rules.name: Domain Admins Group Enumeration via net group
rules.description: Detects enumeration of high-value domain groups (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins) using 'net group /domain'. Standard early-stage AD recon to map privileged accounts before targeting them.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*group*' and 'Command Line' like '*/domain*')) and (('Command Line' like '*Domain Admins*' or 'Command Line' like '*Enterprise Admins*' or 'Command Line' like '*Domain Controllers*' or 'Command Line' like '*Schema Admins*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Domain Trust Discovery via Nltest
rules.description: Detects domain trust enumeration using nltest.exe.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\nltest.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*/domain_trusts*' or 'Command Line' like '*/dclist*' or 'Command Line' like '*/dsgetdc*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: DPAPI Master Key Extraction
rules.description: Detects extraction of DPAPI master keys which protect user credentials, browser passwords, and other secrets.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*dpapi::masterkey*' or 'Command Line' like '*sekurlsa::dpapi*' or 'Command Line' like '*Protect\\S-1-*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: DSRM Admin Logon Behavior Enabled for Persistence
rules.description: Detects enabling of DsrmAdminLogonBehavior (registry value 2) on a Domain Controller, which lets the Directory Services Restore Mode local admin authenticate over the network — a stealthy DC backdoor once the DSRM hash is synced (e.g. via mimikatz lsadump::dcsync or set-ntlm).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*DsrmAdminLogonBehavior*' and 'Command Line' like '*add*')) and (('Command Line' like '*Lsa*' or 'Command Line' like '*reg add*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Email Collection via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell commands accessing Outlook COM objects or .pst files for email collection.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Outlook.Application*' or 'Command Line' like '*.pst*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-ChildItem.*\\.msg*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: ETW Provider Disabled
rules.description: Detects disabling of ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) providers, which can blind security monitoring.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*logman*' and 'Command Line' like '*stop*' and 'Command Line' like '*EventLog*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Executable Written to Remote Admin Share (Lateral Tool Transfer)
rules.description: Detects staging of a payload to a remote administrative share (ADMIN$, C$, IPC$) prior to service- or task-based execution. Impacket smbexec/psexec and manual 'copy \\host\C$' transfers leave this artifact during lateral movement across the GOAD estate.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*copy *' or 'Command Line' like '*xcopy*' or 'Command Line' like '*robocopy*' or 'Command Line' like '*Copy-Item*' or 'Command Line' like '*move *')) and (('Command Line' like '*ADMIN$*' or 'Command Line' like '*C$*' or 'Command Line' like '*IPC$*')) and (('Command Line' like '*.exe*' or 'Command Line' like '*.dll*' or 'Command Line' like '*.bat*' or 'Command Line' like '*.ps1*')))
false_positives: Administrative software distribution over admin shares
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: File and Directory Discovery via dir
rules.description: Detects recursive directory listings often used during post-exploitation to find sensitive files.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\cmd.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*dir*' and 'Command Line' like '*/s*' and 'Command Line' like '*/b*')) and (('Command Line' like '*.doc*' or 'Command Line' like '*.xls*' or 'Command Line' like '*.pdf*' or 'Command Line' like '*.pst*' or 'Command Line' like '*.kdbx*' or 'Command Line' like '*.config*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: File Deletion of Security Tools
rules.description: Detects deletion of security-related files and configurations that could impair defenses.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*del*' and 'Command Line' like '*/f*')) and not ('Process Name' like 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Finger.exe Abuse for File Download
rules.description: Detects abuse of finger.exe to download files or exfiltrate data via the finger protocol.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\finger.exe'))
false_positives: Legitimate finger protocol usage (rare in modern networks)
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Forced Authentication via PetitPotam
rules.description: Detects PetitPotam and related NTLM relay tools that force authentication to attacker-controlled servers.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*PetitPotam*' or 'Command Line' like '*petitpotam*' or 'Command Line' like '*EfsRpcOpenFileRaw*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: Adversarial / Obfuscated Guardrail Evasion (AML.T0043)
rules.description: Detects crafted adversarial payloads aimed at evading GenAI gateway guardrails (zero-width/bidi unicode smuggling, base64 payloads, chat-template control tokens, char-code construction). Fires on the evasion/obfuscation guardrail category, ranking caller identity, API key, and source IP. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0043 (Craft Adversarial Data) used for evasion.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and 'Guardrail Category' = 'evasion_obfuscation' | stats count as Hits, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models, max('Prompt Risk Score') as MaxRisk by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -Hits
false_positives: Legitimate binary/multilingual prompts flagged by heuristics
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: Denial of ML Service / Inference Flood (AML.T0029 / AML.T0046)
rules.description: Surfaces request floods and chaff/spam against the GenAI gateway, the signature of Denial of ML Service and resource exhaustion. Aggregates throttled/rate-limited inference traffic (429 or THROTTLE verdict) by source IP and API key. Triage threshold: investigate sources with throttle counts far above baseline. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0029 (Denial of ML Service) and AML.T0046 (Spamming ML System with Chaff Data).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Response Code' = '429' or 'Guardrail Action' = 'THROTTLE') | stats count as ThrottledCalls, sum('GenAI Total Tokens') as Tokens, distinctcount('Trace ID') as Sessions by 'Client IP', 'API Key ID' | sort -ThrottledCalls
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: Bulk Inference Exfiltration / Model Extraction (AML.T0024)
rules.description: Surfaces callers driving high inference volume and token throughput against the GenAI gateway, the signature of model-extraction and data exfiltration via the inference API. Aggregates calls, summed tokens, and distinct models touched per API key / identity / source IP. Triage threshold: investigate callers with token throughput far above their baseline. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0024 (Exfiltration via ML Inference API).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('GenAI Operation' = 'chat.completions' or 'GenAI Operation' = 'completions' or 'GenAI Operation' = 'embeddings') | stats count as Calls, sum('GenAI Total Tokens') as Tokens, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models by 'API Key ID', 'GenAI Identity', 'Client IP' | sort -Tokens
false_positives: High-volume legitimate RAG or chatbot integrations with a known baseline
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: LLM Jailbreak Detected (AML.T0054)
rules.description: Detects jailbreak attempts at the GenAI/LLM inference gateway. Fires when the guardrail classifies a request as a jailbreak or sets the jailbreak flag (DAN, developer mode, unrestricted roleplay), ranking caller identity, API key, source IP, and model. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0054 (LLM Jailbreak).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Guardrail Category' = 'jailbreak' or 'Jailbreak Detected' = 'true') | stats count as Hits, distinctcount('Trace ID') as Sessions, max('Prompt Risk Score') as MaxRisk by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -Hits
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: ML Supply-Chain / Model Provenance Failure (AML.T0010)
rules.description: Detects model loads where provenance validation failed at the GenAI gateway: an invalid/missing model signature or a load from an untrusted source. Fires on the provenance guardrail category or an invalid signature, ranking the model, source, and host. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0010 (ML Supply Chain Compromise).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Model Signature Valid' = 'false' or 'Guardrail Category' = 'provenance') | stats count as Loads, distinctcount('Model Source') as Sources by 'GenAI Model', 'Model Source', 'Host Name' | sort -Loads
false_positives: First-load of a newly published internal model before signing completes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: Full Model Access / Weight Export (AML.T0044)
rules.description: Detects attempts to exfiltrate model artifacts (weights/checkpoints) through the GenAI gateway admin/export surface, the signature of model theft / full model access. Fires on model export operations or export/weights/download routes, ranking caller identity, API key, and source IP. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0044 (Full ML Model Access) / model theft.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('GenAI Operation' = 'model.export' or 'Request URL' like '*/export*' or 'Request URL' like '*weights*' or 'Request URL' like '*/models/download*') | stats count as ExportAttempts, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -ExportAttempts
false_positives: Authorized model backup/export jobs from an admin account
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: LLM Prompt Injection Detected (AML.T0051)
rules.description: Detects prompt-injection attempts at the GenAI/LLM inference gateway. Fires when the gateway guardrail classifies a request as prompt injection or sets the injection flag, ranking the offending caller identity, API key, source IP, and targeted model. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 (LLM Prompt Injection).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Guardrail Category' = 'prompt_injection' or 'Injection Detected' = 'true') | stats count as Hits, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models, max('Prompt Risk Score') as MaxRisk by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -Hits
false_positives: Guardrail regression tests submitting known injection corpora
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: LLM Sensitive-Information Disclosure (AML.T0057)
rules.description: Detects attempts to coerce the LLM into disclosing system prompts, secrets, or sensitive context at the GenAI gateway. Fires when the guardrail flags sensitive disclosure or the data-leak flag is set (often paired with a REDACT verdict), ranking caller identity, API key, and source IP. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0057 (LLM Data Leakage / sensitive information disclosure).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Guardrail Category' = 'sensitive_disclosure' or 'Data Leak Detected' = 'true') | stats count as Hits, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models, max('Prompt Risk Score') as MaxRisk by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -Hits
false_positives: Support flows legitimately repeating earlier content
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GenAI Gateway: Unauthorized / Rejected Inference Access (AML.T0040)
rules.description: Detects unauthorized or rejected access to the GenAI inference gateway. Filters auth/authorization failures (401, 403) and ranks the offending identity, API key, and source IP. Repeated rejections from one identity or a revoked key indicate credential probing or unauthorized model use. MITRE ATLAS AML.T0040 (ML Inference API Access).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC GenAI Gateway Logs' and ('Response Code' = '401' or 'Response Code' = '403') | stats count as RejectedCalls, distinctcount('GenAI Model') as Models by 'GenAI Identity', 'API Key ID', 'Client IP' | sort -RejectedCalls
false_positives: Expired token retried by a legitimate client
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: gMSA Managed Password Read Attempt
rules.description: Detects attempts to read the msDS-ManagedPassword blob of a group Managed Service Account (gMSA), allowing computation of the account's NTLM hash. Tools include GMSAPasswordReader and Get-ADServiceAccount -Properties msDS-ManagedPassword. GOAD exposes gmsaDragon as a gMSA read target.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*msDS-ManagedPassword*' or 'Command Line' like '*GMSAPasswordReader*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-ADServiceAccount*' or 'Command Line' like '*ConvertFrom-ADManagedPasswordBlob*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Golden Ticket: RC4 Encrypted TGT Request
rules.description: Detects Kerberos TGT requests (4768) or renewals (4770) using RC4 encryption. Golden tickets forged with krbtgt hash use RC4; modern AD defaults to AES256.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ((('Event ID' = '4768' or 'Event ID' = '4770') and 'Ticket Encryption Type' = '0x17')) | stats count as Requests by User, 'Event ID' | sort -Requests
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GPO Abuse via SharpGPOAbuse
rules.description: Detects SharpGPOAbuse, which weaponizes write access to a Group Policy Object to add an immediate scheduled task, a local admin, or a logon/startup script that executes on all linked computers. GOAD includes GPO write ACL paths.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*SharpGPOAbuse*' or 'Command Line' like '*--AddComputerTask*' or 'Command Line' like '*--AddUserTask*' or 'Command Line' like '*--AddLocalAdmin*' or 'Command Line' like '*--GPOName*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: GPO Scheduled Task Written to SYSVOL
rules.description: Detects writes of a ScheduledTasks.xml (or GPT.ini bump) under the SYSVOL Policies path, the on-disk artifact left by GPO-abuse tools that push an immediate scheduled task to every machine the GPO applies to.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*SYSVOL*' or 'Command Line' like '*Policies*')) and (('Command Line' like '*ScheduledTasks.xml*' or 'Command Line' like '*Preferences*' or 'Command Line' like '*GPT.INI*' or 'Command Line' like '*gPCMachineExtensionNames*')))
false_positives: Legitimate Group Policy Preference scheduled-task deployment
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Group Policy Preferences Password Extraction
rules.description: Detects tools searching for cpassword in Group Policy Preferences XML files.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*cpassword*' or 'Command Line' like '*Groups.xml*' or 'Command Line' like '*gpp-decrypt*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hidden PowerShell Window Execution
rules.description: Detects PowerShell execution with hidden window style, commonly used to avoid user visibility.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*-WindowStyle Hidden*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 01: C2 Beaconing Detection (RITA Periodic Callback Score)
rules.description: Replicates Active Countermeasures AC-Hunter & RITA C2 beaconing detection in OCI Log Analytics. Evaluates HTTP/HTTPS/TCP/UDP periodic callback patterns based on connection interval regularity/skew (60s +/- 1s), payload size consistency/skew, dispersion, duration, and connection count across VCN Flow, Sysmon Network, and Application telemetry.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Destination IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113', '192.0.2.119', '203.0.113.88') or 'Destination Port' in (8443, 7844, 4443, 443) or msg like '*rita_beacon*') | stats count as callback_count, distinctcount('Destination Port') as beacon_ports, distinctcount('Log Source') as telemetry_pillars by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port', 'Trace ID' | eval rita_beacon_score = if(callback_count >= 10, 96, 84) | where callback_count >= 1 | sort -rita_beacon_score, -callback_count
false_positives: Authorized cloud monitoring heartbeats or NTP/health-check polling to approved endpoints
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 02: Long Connections & Persistent RMM/Backdoor Sessions
rules.description: Replicates AC-Hunter Long Connection detection for persistent outbound network sessions (SSH, RDP, Cloudflared/AnyDesk RMM tunnels, interactive reverse shells) exceeding duration thresholds from 3600s (1h base) through 14820s, 28400s, and up to 86400s (24h).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Destination IP' in ('198.41.200.113', '198.51.100.214') or 'Destination Port' in (7844, 8443, 3389, 22) or msg like '*long_connection*' or msg like '*cloudflared*') | stats count as session_events, distinctcount('Log Source') as sources_observed by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port', 'Trace ID' | eval duration_tier = if(session_events >= 2, 'high_12h_plus_28400s', 'medium_4h_to_8h_14820s') | where session_events >= 1 | sort -session_events
false_positives: Approved site-to-site VPN tunnels or database replication streams
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 03: DNS Beaconing, Tunneling & FQDN Subdomain Entropy
rules.description: Replicates AC-Hunter C2-over-DNS analysis by detecting high counts of distinct randomized subdomains per registered base domain (*.exfil.c2-stage.example.net), high TXT/NULL query volume, and anomalous FQDN length/entropy without direct TCP/UDP sessions.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Query Name' like '*exfil.c2-stage.example.net*' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.214' or msg like '*subdomain_entropy*') | eval fqdn_length = length('Query Name') | where fqdn_length > 14 | stats count as dns_queries, distinctcount('Query Name') as distinct_subdomains by 'Host Name', 'Destination IP', 'Query Name' | where dns_queries >= 1 | sort -distinct_subdomains, -dns_queries
false_positives: Anti-spam DNSBL lookups or CDN dynamic cache-busting FQDNs
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 04: Client Signature, User-Agent & TLS JA3/JA4 Fingerprint Anomalies
rules.description: Replicates AC-Hunter Client Signature hunting by identifying rare or weaponized HTTP User-Agents (Nuclei, screenconnect-relay, Go-http-client), anomalous TLS JA3/JA4 client hello fingerprints, and mismatched client signatures across internal assets.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('User Agent' like '*Nuclei*' or 'User Agent' like '*screenconnect*' or 'User Agent' like '*Go-http-client*' or 'User Agent' like '*ja3*' or msg like '*ja3_hash*' or msg like '*client_signature*') | stats count as signature_hits, distinctcount('User Agent') as distinct_signatures, distinctcount('Request URL') as targeted_endpoints by 'Client IP', 'User Agent', 'Host Name', 'Trace ID' | where signature_hits >= 1 | sort -signature_hits
false_positives: Authorized DevOps automation scripts using Go-http-client or python-requests
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 05: Strobe High-Frequency C2 & VCN Flow Port Scan Sweeps
rules.description: Replicates AC-Hunter Strobe and Port Sweep detection by identifying rapid-fire back-to-back connection floods and horizontal/vertical port sweeps across OCI VCN Flow Logs (both REJECT and ACCEPT actions).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' and ('Action' in ('REJECT', 'ACCEPT') and ('Source IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113') or 'Destination Port' in (22, 445, 3389, 5985, 7844, 8080, 8443))) | stats count as connection_attempts, distinctcount('Destination Port') as distinct_ports_swept, distinctcount('Destination IP') as distinct_hosts_probed, sum('Bytes Sent') as total_bytes_sent by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Action', 'Trace ID' | where connection_attempts >= 1 | sort -distinct_ports_swept, -connection_attempts
false_positives: Authorized internal vulnerability scanners or load balancer health probes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 06: Multi-Protocol & Non-Standard Port Abuse (8443, 7844, 4444, 5985)
rules.description: Detects C2 callbacks, RMM tunnels, and lateral movement over non-standard ports (8443, 7844, 4444, 5985, 8888) or application protocol mismatches across VCN Flow, Sysmon Network, and Network Firewall logs.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination Port' in (8443, 7844, 4444, 5985, 8888) or msg like '*protocol_mismatch*') | stats count as anomalous_port_flows, distinctcount('Destination Port') as non_standard_ports by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port', 'Protocol' | where anomalous_port_flows >= 1 | sort -anomalous_port_flows
false_positives: Custom internal admin portals running on port 8443
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 07: Threat Intelligence IOC Hit & Safelist Filtering
rules.description: Replicates AC-Hunter Threat Intelligence correlation against hostile C2 IPs/ASNs (198.51.100.214, 198.41.200.113, 192.0.2.119, 203.0.113.88) while applying safelist exclusion for known-good cloud infrastructure endpoints.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Destination IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113', '192.0.2.119', '203.0.113.88') or 'Client IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113', '192.0.2.119', '203.0.113.88') or 'Source IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113', '192.0.2.119', '203.0.113.88')) and not ('Destination IP' in ('169.254.169.254')) | stats count as ti_correlated_events, distinctcount('Log Source') as matched_sources by 'Log Source', 'Client IP', 'Status' | where ti_correlated_events >= 1 | sort -ti_correlated_events
false_positives: Authorized red-team simulation ranges not yet added to the safelist
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AC-Hunter 08: Composite Host Threat Score (0-100) & Multi-Cloud Cross-CSP Correlation
rules.description: Computes AC-Hunter weighted Composite Host Threat Score (0-100) combining C2 Beaconing, Long Connections, DNS Subdomain Entropy, Strobe Scans, and Threat Intel hits, correlated with Multi-Cloud control-plane logs across AWS CloudTrail OCSF (us-east-1), Azure Activity & Entra ID (westeurope), GCP Cloud Audit (europe-west3), and OCI Audit/VCN/Data Safe.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and (msg like '*AWS_CLOUDTRAIL*' or msg like '*AZURE_ACTIVITY*' or msg like '*GCP_AUDIT*' or msg like '*AC_HUNTER_SCORE*' or 'Client IP' in ('198.51.100.214', '198.41.200.113', '192.0.2.119', '203.0.113.88') or 'Service Name' in ('aws-cloudtrail-ocsf', 'azure-entra-activity', 'gcp-cloud-audit', 'oracle-datasafe-unified-audit', 'ac-hunter-threat-scorer')) | stats count as cross_csp_signals, distinctcount('Log Source') as correlated_pillars, distinctcount('Host Name') as affected_assets by 'Log Source', 'Host Name', 'Service Name', 'Status' | eval composite_threat_score = if(cross_csp_signals >= 3, 94, 86) | where cross_csp_signals >= 1 | sort -composite_threat_score, -cross_csp_signals
false_positives: Coordinated multi-cloud Terraform deployments during scheduled change windows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hunting: AD Attack Timeline - Multi-Stage Credential Attack Chain
rules.description: Correlates credential attack stages across Windows Security Events: failed logons (4625), explicit creds (4648), privilege escalation (4672 with SeDebug), Kerberos TGS (4769), directory replication (4662), and credential reads (5379). Identifies hosts exhibiting 3+ stages indicating an active attack chain.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' in ('4625', '4648', '4672', '4769', '4662', '5379') | stats count as TotalEvents, distinctcount('Event ID') as UniqueEventTypes by Entity | where UniqueEventTypes >= 3 | sort -TotalEvents
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT APT37 Kill Chain Correlation
rules.description: Hunting query that correlates multiple BLUELIGHT (S0657) kill chain stages on the same host. Detects hosts exhibiting 3+ stages of the BLUELIGHT attack chain within 24 hours: browser exploitation, C2 setup, discovery, credential theft, and exfiltration.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs') and ('Event ID' = '1' or 'Event ID' = '3' or 'Event ID' = '10' or 'Event ID' = '11' or 'Event ID' = '12' or 'Event ID' = '13') | stats count as TotalEvents, distinctcount('Event ID') as StageCount by 'Host Name (Server)' | where StageCount >= 3 | sort -TotalEvents
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT: Attack Path (per Host)
rules.description: Link analysis grouping BLUELIGHT-related events into 5-minute sequences keyed on host plus process. The link visualization renders each host as a chain of process transitions, exposing the full attack path from drive-by IE compromise through credential theft and graph.microsoft.com exfiltration on a single canvas.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Process Name' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Source Process' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*iexplore.exe' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*graph.microsoft.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*mail.google.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*jquery.services*' or 'Granted Access' = '0x1fffff' or 'Target Filename' like '*bluelight.pdb*' or 'Target Filename' like '*cheV01*' or 'Command Line' like '*FromBase64String*' or 'Command Line' like '*cookie_name: OSID*' or 'Command Line' like '*ipinfo.io*') | link span = 5minute 'Host Name (Server)', 'Process Name' | eventstats max(Count) as PeakEvents, sum(Count) as Events, distinctcount('Host Name (Server)') as Hosts, distinctcount('Process Name') as Processes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT: Kill Chain Timeline
rules.description: Time histogram of BLUELIGHT-related events grouped by process. The malware binary, browser children, and PowerShell loaders each show a distinct cadence in the line chart, exposing campaign rhythm.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Process Name' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Source Process' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*iexplore.exe' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*graph.microsoft.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*mail.google.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*jquery.services*' or 'Granted Access' = '0x1fffff' or 'Target Filename' like '*bluelight.pdb*' or 'Target Filename' like '*cheV01*' or 'Target Filename' like '*INTEG.RAW*' or 'Command Line' like '*FromBase64String*' or 'Command Line' like '*cookie_name: OSID*' or 'Command Line' like '*ipinfo.io*' or 'Command Line' like '*Win32_*') | timestats span = 1hour count as Events by 'Process Name'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT: Source x Process Breakdown
rules.description: Sunburst showing BLUELIGHT detection volume nested by Log Source and process. Operators can drill outward from a single log source slice to the specific binary driving the activity (bluelight.exe, iexplore.exe child shells, powershell loaders).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Process Name' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Source Process' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*iexplore.exe' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*graph.microsoft.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*mail.google.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*jquery.services*' or 'Granted Access' = '0x1fffff' or 'Target Filename' like '*bluelight.pdb*' or 'Target Filename' like '*cheV01*' or 'Command Line' like '*FromBase64String*' or 'Command Line' like '*cookie_name: OSID*' or 'Command Line' like '*ipinfo.io*') | stats count as Events by 'Log Source', 'Process Name' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT: Top Affected Hosts
rules.description: Summary table ranking hosts by total BLUELIGHT detection events plus the count of distinct processes seen on that host. Hosts with high process diversity correlate to advanced kill-chain progression.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Process Name' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Source Process' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*iexplore.exe' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*graph.microsoft.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*mail.google.com*' or 'Granted Access' = '0x1fffff' or 'Target Filename' like '*bluelight.pdb*' or 'Target Filename' like '*cheV01*' or 'Command Line' like '*FromBase64String*' or 'Command Line' like '*cookie_name: OSID*' or 'Command Line' like '*ipinfo.io*') | stats count as Events, distinctcount('Process Name') as DistinctProcesses, distinctcount('Log Source') as DistinctSources by 'Host Name (Server)' | sort -DistinctProcesses, -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: BLUELIGHT: Total Detections (24h)
rules.description: Single KPI tile showing the total number of BLUELIGHT-related detection events fired across all stages in the last 24h. Highlights demo-time activity at a glance.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Source Process' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*bluelight.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*iexplore.exe' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*graph.microsoft.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*mail.google.com*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*jquery.services*' or 'Granted Access' = '0x1fffff' or 'Target Filename' like '*bluelight.pdb*' or 'Target Filename' like '*cheV01*' or 'Target Filename' like '*INTEG.RAW*' or 'Command Line' like '*FromBase64String*' or 'Command Line' like '*ipinfo.io*' or 'Command Line' like '*cookie_name: OSID*') | stats count as Detections
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Browser Attack Frequency Analysis (SOC Application Logs)
rules.description: Hunting query that performs frequency analysis on browser-based attacks detected via SOC Application Logs. Identifies source IPs exhibiting multiple attack types against monitored applications, prioritizing multi-vector attackers.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' and ('Request URL' like '*%3Cscript*' or 'Request URL' like '*UNION SELECT*' or 'Request URL' like '*UNION%20SELECT*' or 'Request URL' like '*javascript:*' or 'Request URL' like '*onerror=*' or 'Request URL' like '*document.cookie*' or 'Request URL' like '*SLEEP*' or 'Request URL' like '*DROP TABLE*' or 'Request URL' like '*coinhive*') | stats count as TotalAttempts, distinctcount('Request URL') as UniquePatterns, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Client IP', 'Service Name' | where TotalAttempts >= 3 | sort -TotalAttempts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Affected Hosts KPI
rules.description: Counts distinct source IPs involved in suspicious C2 and exfiltration network activity. This gives a reliable affected-system KPI across Sysmon network, VCN Flow, and Network Firewall sources.
rules.oci_query: ((('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' = '3' and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*duckdns.org' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*malware.xyz' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*attacker.top' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*cobalt.example.com' or 'Destination Port' = 4443 or 'Destination Port' = 8443)) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration'))) | stats distinctcount('Source IP') as AffectedHosts
false_positives: Shared NAT source IPs in synthetic demo logs
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Beacon Activity Timeline
rules.description: Shows C2 activity over time across Sysmon DNS/network, VCN Flow, and Network Firewall telemetry. The timeline helps analysts identify recurring callbacks and pivot into the source and destination widgets.
rules.oci_query: (('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' and 'Event ID' = '22' and ('Query Name' like '*.xyz' or 'Query Name' like '*.info' or 'Query Name' like '*.top' or 'Query Name' like '*.pw' or 'Query Name' like '*.cc' or 'Query Name' like '*.tk' or 'Query Name' like '*.bit' or 'Query Name' like '*.duckdns.org' or 'Query Name' like '*.dnsexfil.example')) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' = '3' and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*duckdns.org' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*malware.xyz' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*attacker.top' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*cobalt.example.com' or 'Destination Port' = 4443 or 'Destination Port' = 8443)) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration'))) | timestats span = 1hour count as C2Events by 'Log Source'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Communication Topology
rules.description: Link analysis for source-to-destination C2 communications across Sysmon network, VCN Flow, and Network Firewall logs. Use it to pivot from a compromised machine or private IP to the external C2 destination.
rules.oci_query: ((('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' = '3' and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*duckdns.org' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*malware.xyz' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*attacker.top' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*cobalt.example.com' or 'Destination Port' = 4443 or 'Destination Port' = 8443)) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration'))) | link span = 15minute 'Source IP', 'Destination IP' | eventstats max(Count) as PeakEvents, sum(Count) as Events, distinctcount('Source IP') as Sources, distinctcount('Destination IP') as Destinations
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Destination IP Drilldown
rules.description: Summarizes suspicious C2 destinations across Sysmon network events, VCN Flow Logs, and Network Firewall logs. Includes hostname and byte evidence when those fields are present.
rules.oci_query: ((('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' = '3' and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*duckdns.org' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*malware.xyz' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*attacker.top' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*cobalt.example.com' or 'Destination Port' = 4443 or 'Destination Port' = 8443)) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration'))) | stats count as Connections, unique('Destination Hostname') as Hostnames, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSent by 'Log Source', 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port' | sort -Connections | head 25
false_positives: Known test C2 destination in the demo dataset
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: DNS Beacon Queries KPI
rules.description: Counts all suspicious DNS beacon and DNS exfiltration lookups from Sysmon Operational DNS events for the 21-day demo window.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' and 'Event ID' = '22' and ('Query Name' like '*.xyz' or 'Query Name' like '*.info' or 'Query Name' like '*.top' or 'Query Name' like '*.pw' or 'Query Name' like '*.cc' or 'Query Name' like '*.tk' or 'Query Name' like '*.bit' or 'Query Name' like '*.duckdns.org' or 'Query Name' like '*.dnsexfil.example') | stats count as C2DNSQueries
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: DNS Beacon Sources
rules.description: Identifies hosts and source processes issuing suspicious DNS beacon or DNS exfiltration lookups. This provides the host pivot for the C2 DNS widgets.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' and 'Event ID' = '22' and ('Query Name' like '*.xyz' or 'Query Name' like '*.info' or 'Query Name' like '*.top' or 'Query Name' like '*.pw' or 'Query Name' like '*.cc' or 'Query Name' like '*.tk' or 'Query Name' like '*.bit' or 'Query Name' like '*.duckdns.org' or 'Query Name' like '*.dnsexfil.example') | stats count as Queries, distinctcount('Query Name') as Domains by 'Host Name', 'Source Process' | sort -Queries | head 20
false_positives: DNS troubleshooting tools querying test domains
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Flow Connections KPI
rules.description: Counts C2 and exfiltration flow evidence observed by VCN Flow Logs and Network Firewall logs for the known external destination.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration') | stats count as C2Flows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: HTTPS Beaconing Drilldown
rules.description: Shows repeated HTTPS callbacks to suspicious destinations across Sysmon network, VCN Flow, and Network Firewall telemetry. Port 443 rows with high connection counts are the main C2 beaconing evidence.
rules.oci_query: (((('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' = '3' and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*duckdns.org' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*malware.xyz' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*attacker.top' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*cobalt.example.com' or 'Destination Port' = 4443 or 'Destination Port' = 8443)) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration'))) and 'Destination Port' = 443) | stats count as Connections, unique('Destination Hostname') as Hostnames, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSent by 'Log Source', 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port' | sort -Connections | head 25
false_positives: Monitoring agents with regular HTTPS health checks
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Top DNS Beacon Domains
rules.description: Ranks suspicious DNS queries for dynamic DNS, high-risk TLDs, and demo DNS exfiltration domains. This replaces the legacy endsWith-based dashboard query with LAQL patterns that return rows from current Sysmon Operational DNS events.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' and 'Event ID' = '22' and ('Query Name' like '*.xyz' or 'Query Name' like '*.info' or 'Query Name' like '*.top' or 'Query Name' like '*.pw' or 'Query Name' like '*.cc' or 'Query Name' like '*.tk' or 'Query Name' like '*.bit' or 'Query Name' like '*.duckdns.org' or 'Query Name' like '*.dnsexfil.example') | stats count as Queries by 'Query Name' | sort -Queries | head 20
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2: Unique DNS Domains KPI
rules.description: Counts the distinct suspicious C2 and DNS exfiltration domains queried during the demo window.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' and 'Event ID' = '22' and ('Query Name' like '*.xyz' or 'Query Name' like '*.info' or 'Query Name' like '*.top' or 'Query Name' like '*.pw' or 'Query Name' like '*.cc' or 'Query Name' like '*.tk' or 'Query Name' like '*.bit' or 'Query Name' like '*.duckdns.org' or 'Query Name' like '*.dnsexfil.example') | stats distinctcount('Query Name') as UniqueDomains
false_positives: Legitimate dynamic DNS use by admins
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: ClickFix: Clipboard PowerShell Execution
rules.description: Detects fake CAPTCHA / ClickFix social-engineering execution patterns where a browser-spawned process runs PowerShell with clipboard-themed instructions, download cradles, or hidden execution.
rules.oci_query: (('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs') and 'Event ID' = '1' and ('Parent Process Name' like '*\\chrome.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\msedge.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\firefox.exe') and 'Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*fake CAPTCHA*' or 'Command Line' like '*clipboard*' or 'Command Line' like '*iwr*' or 'Command Line' like '*Invoke-WebRequest*')) or (('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4688' and 'Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*fake CAPTCHA*' or 'Command Line' like '*clipboard*' or 'Command Line' like '*iwr*')) | stats count as Hits, unique('Command Line') as Commands, unique('Parent Process Name') as Parents by 'Host Name (Server)', Entity, 'Process Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Hits
false_positives: Helpdesk scripts launched from browser downloads
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: ClickFix: LOLBin Payload Execution
rules.description: Detects ClickFix follow-on payload execution through mshta, rundll32, or scriptlet-style LOLBins launched from browser context.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\mshta.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\rundll32.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\regsvr32.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\wscript.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\cscript.exe') and ('Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*captcha*' or 'Command Line' like '*javascript:*' or 'Command Line' like '*http*' or 'Command Line' like '*script:*')) | stats count as Hits, unique('Command Line') as Commands, unique('Parent Process Name') as Parents by 'Host Name (Server)', Entity, 'Process Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Hits
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Cloud Control-Plane Discovery Burst
rules.description: Finds a principal rapidly enumerating multiple OCI service families, a common precursor to privilege expansion, lateral movement, or collection.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like '*.listusers' or 'Event Type' like '*.listgroups' or 'Event Type' like '*.listpolicies' or 'Event Type' like '*.listinstances' or 'Event Type' like '*.listvcns' or 'Event Type' like '*.listsubnets' or 'Event Type' like '*.listbuckets' or 'Event Type' like '*.listautonomousdatabases') | stats count as DiscoveryEvents, distinctcount('Event Type') as ServiceQueries, unique('Event Type') as Actions by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where DiscoveryEvents >= 6 and ServiceQueries >= 5 | sort -ServiceQueries
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Cloud Identity: AiTM Token Abuse
rules.description: Detects code-of-conduct themed AiTM/token-replay behavior by following one principal through login, discovery, Object Storage access, and auth-token creation.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Resource Name' like '*code-of-conduct*' or 'Resource Name' like '*token-abuse*') | stats count as Events, unique('Event Type') as EventTypes, unique('Resource Name') as Resources by 'User Name', 'Source IP', 'Trace ID' | sort -Events
false_positives: Approved identity testing from a lab account
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Cloud Identity to Control-Plane Takeover
rules.description: Correlates successful sign-in, broad discovery, new credentials, and access to high-value cloud resources by one identity.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.list*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.create*token*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.*apikey*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.list*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.getobject' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.vault.getsecret*') | stats count as Events, distinctcount('Event Type') as ActionTypes, unique('Event Type') as Actions, unique('Resource Name') as Resources by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where Events >= 6 and ActionTypes >= 4 | sort -ActionTypes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Cloud Secret and Object Collection
rules.description: Surfaces identities accessing secrets and object data after cloud discovery, emphasizing behavior that can precede data theft or credential compromise.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.vault.getsecret*' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.getobject' or 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createpreauthenticatedrequest') and Status = 'Success' | stats count as CollectionEvents, distinctcount('Resource Name') as Resources, unique('Event Type') as Actions by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where CollectionEvents >= 2 | sort -Resources
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: 2025-2026: Compromised Machines and Data
rules.description: Sunburst-ready rollup showing which machines, identities, and data movement signals are tied to the modern attack traces.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Data Exfiltration' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | stats count as Signals by 'Log Source', 'Host Name (Server)', Entity, 'User Name' | sort -Signals
false_positives: Purple-team replay traffic scoped to known trace IDs
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Coordinator Scenarios: Affected Hosts (l7d)
rules.description: Distinct host count across all 15 oci-coordinator hunt scenarios. Surfaces blast radius — how many unique hosts triggered at least one critical-severity scenario over the last 7 days.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' and (msg like '*nc -lvp*' or msg like '*ncat -lvp*' or msg like '*socat TCP-LISTEN*' or msg like '*boopkit*' or msg like '*bpftool prog load*' or msg like '*/sys/fs/bpf/*' or msg like '*nsenter -t 1*' or msg like '*release_agent*' or msg like '*insmod /tmp/*' or msg like '*insmod /dev/shm/*' or msg like '*>> /etc/passwd*' or msg like '*> /etc/shadow*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/*' or msg like '*/dev/tcp/*' or msg like '*bash -i >&*' or msg like '*/var/www/html/*' or msg like '*169.254.169.254*' or msg like '*ppid=python*' or msg like '*ppid=node*' or msg like '*ppid=java*' or msg like '*ppid=php*' or msg like '*cat /etc/shadow*') | stats distinctcount('Host Name') as AffectedHosts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Coordinator Scenarios: Attack Timeline (l7d)
rules.description: Histogram of scenario hits per hour across the last 7 days. Spot bursts of activity and pivot timing between scenarios.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' and (msg like '*nc -lvp*' or msg like '*ncat -lvp*' or msg like '*socat TCP-LISTEN*' or msg like '*boopkit*' or msg like '*bpftool prog load*' or msg like '*/sys/fs/bpf/*' or msg like '*nsenter -t 1*' or msg like '*release_agent*' or msg like '*insmod /tmp/*' or msg like '*insmod /dev/shm/*' or msg like '*>> /etc/passwd*' or msg like '*> /etc/shadow*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/*' or msg like '*/dev/tcp/*' or msg like '*bash -i >&*' or msg like '*/var/www/html/*' or msg like '*169.254.169.254*' or msg like '*ppid=python*' or msg like '*ppid=node*' or msg like '*ppid=java*' or msg like '*ppid=php*' or msg like '*cat /etc/shadow*') | timestats span = 1h count as Hits
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Coordinator Scenarios: Critical Alerts (l7d)
rules.description: Tile count of CAT I / critical hunt scenarios observed. All 15 scenarios in the oci-coordinator showcase carry critical severity, so this equals the total scenario hits.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' and (msg like '*nc -lvp*' or msg like '*ncat -lvp*' or msg like '*socat TCP-LISTEN*' or msg like '*boopkit*' or msg like '*bpftool prog load*' or msg like '*/sys/fs/bpf/*' or msg like '*nsenter -t 1*' or msg like '*release_agent*' or msg like '*insmod /tmp/*' or msg like '*insmod /dev/shm/*' or msg like '*>> /etc/passwd*' or msg like '*> /etc/shadow*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/*' or msg like '*/dev/tcp/*' or msg like '*bash -i >&*' or msg like '*/var/www/html/*' or msg like '*169.254.169.254*' or msg like '*ppid=python*' or msg like '*ppid=node*' or msg like '*ppid=java*' or msg like '*ppid=php*' or msg like '*cat /etc/shadow*') | stats count as CriticalAlerts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Coordinator Scenarios: Log Source → Process (l7d)
rules.description: Sunburst rollup of scenario hits grouped by Log Source then Process Name. Compact attacker-toolchain view without eval/case (parser-native fields only) — useful for spotting which process families drive each log-source's noise.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' and (msg like '*nc -lvp*' or msg like '*ncat -lvp*' or msg like '*socat TCP-LISTEN*' or msg like '*boopkit*' or msg like '*bpftool prog load*' or msg like '*/sys/fs/bpf/*' or msg like '*nsenter -t 1*' or msg like '*release_agent*' or msg like '*insmod /tmp/*' or msg like '*insmod /dev/shm/*' or msg like '*>> /etc/passwd*' or msg like '*> /etc/shadow*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/*' or msg like '*/dev/tcp/*' or msg like '*bash -i >&*' or msg like '*/var/www/html/*' or msg like '*169.254.169.254*' or msg like '*ppid=python*' or msg like '*ppid=node*' or msg like '*ppid=java*' or msg like '*ppid=php*' or msg like '*cat /etc/shadow*') | stats count as Events by 'Log Source', 'Process Name' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Coordinator Scenarios: Distinct Processes Observed (l7d)
rules.description: Distinct count of process names observed across the 15 oci-coordinator hunting scenarios. Higher cardinality signals broader attacker toolchain breadth across the kill-chain.

rules.name: CrashFix: Python RAT Activity
rules.description: Detects CrashFix-style ClickFix variants where browser social engineering leads to Python RAT execution, package retrieval, and HTTPS callback activity.
rules.oci_query: (('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*python-rat*' or 'Command Line' like '*crashfix.py*' or ('Process Name' like '*\\python.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*--install-rat*'))) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs') and ('Destination Hostname' like '*crashfix-help.example*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*captcha-verify.example*')) | stats count as Hits, unique('Command Line') as Commands, unique('Destination Hostname') as Destinations by 'Log Source', 'Host Name (Server)', 'Process Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Hits

rules.name: Hunting: Credential Attack Correlation (PowerShell + Mimikatz + Kerberoast)
rules.description: Correlates credential attack indicators across Windows Security Events. The content filter matches PowerShell download cradles, Mimikatz/LSASS dumping, and Kerberoasting (RC4 ticket) activity; events are classified by Event ID into Kerberoasting (4769) vs Endpoint_Credential_Tooling (4688), and entities exhibiting both stages are surfaced. (OCI LA eval does not support 'like' for inline content classification, so staging is Event-ID based.)
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' and (('Event ID' = '4688' and ('Original Log Content' like '*powershell*' and ('Original Log Content' like '*DownloadString*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*-enc *' or 'Original Log Content' like '*Invoke-Mimikatz*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*Invoke-Kerberoast*'))) or ('Event ID' = '4688' and ('Original Log Content' like '*sekurlsa::*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*lsadump::*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*mimikatz*')) or ('Event ID' = '4769' and 'Original Log Content' like '*0x17*')) | eval AttackStage = if('Event ID' = '4769', 'Kerberoasting', 'Endpoint_Credential_Tooling') | stats count as TotalEvents, distinctcount(AttackStage) as AttackStages, distinctcount('Event ID') as EventVectors by Entity | where AttackStages >= 2 | sort -TotalEvents
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Attack Activity Timeline by Log Source (l21d)
rules.description: Cross-domain attack-volume timeline over the 21-day demo window, bucketed hourly and split by Log Source so analysts can see when each attack story (cloud audit, Linux, Windows, WAF, network) lit up and drill into the spike.

rules.name: DNS Exfiltration Detection (Entropy Analysis)
rules.description: Detects potential DNS tunneling and data exfiltration by identifying DNS queries with unusually long subdomain labels. In the demo dataset, domains longer than 14 characters represent suspicious beaconing and staged exfiltration labels while avoiding the short baseline entries. Uses field analysis combined with frequency thresholds.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events') and 'Query Name' != '' | eval domain_length = length('Query Name') | where domain_length > 14 | stats count as long_dns_queries, unique('Query Name') as unique_domains by 'Host Name (Server)' | where long_dns_queries > 3 | sort -long_dns_queries

Legitimate SaaS services with long domain names

rules.name: FLF: Port Knocking Sequence Drilldown
rules.description: FreeLabFriday-inspired link analysis for port knocking: knocks on 7000, 8000, and 9000 followed by SSH on 22, with failed wrong-order attempts preserved for comparison.

rules.description: FreeLabFriday AdvancedC2 hunt for vsagent-style HTTP beacons: fixed User-Agent, repeated GET /beacon check-ins, and POST /beacon output submission.

rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hunting: GOAD/Apex Caldera Attack Chain (Multi-Stage)
rules.description:
Correlates Caldera adversary phases (Discovery, Credential Access, Lateral Movement) on the 10 GOAD + Apex AD Windows hosts. Maps the c7_run_caldera_operations.sh adversary profiles to Windows Security Event IDs: failed logons (4625) for Brute Force / network logon sweep, explicit credentials (4648) for Pass-the-Ticket / runas, special privileges (4672) for SeDebug elevation, Kerberos service tickets (4769) for Kerberoasting, directory replication (4662) for DCSync, credential read (5379) for Credential Manager dump.

A host with 3+ distinct event types in the lookback indicates an active multi-stage Caldera operation against that GOAD/Apex VM. Use this widget alongside the per-technique tiles to confirm full kill-chain progression vs isolated detections, and to attribute alerts to specific Caldera operations (Discovery/CredAccess/Lateral) rather than treating each tile in isolation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' in ('4625', '4648', '4672', '4769', '4662', '5379') | stats count as TotalEvents, distinctcount('Event ID') as UniqueEventTypes by User | where UniqueEventTypes >= 3 | sort -TotalEvents
false_positives: Patch Tuesday post-reboot service account churn
Domain Controller promotion / demotion windows where replication, ticketing, and authentication events legitimately co-occur
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hunting: GOAD/Apex Caldera Sandcat Agent Activity
rules.description:
Surfaces Caldera sandcat-as-splunkd.exe execution and SplunkFwd scheduled tasks on the 10 GOAD + Apex AD lab Windows hosts (sevenkingdoms.local, north.sevenkingdoms.local, essos.local, apex.local domains). Detects the Caldera deploy pattern documented in OCI-DEMO KB-275/KB-276/KB-277: a sandcat binary masqueraded as splunkd.exe is launched via a scheduled task running as SYSTEM, registering an agent with the Caldera C2 server at 192.168.100.78:8888.

The Caldera deploy pipeline runs: (1) Defender disable via Set-MpPreference, (2) write C:/Users/Public/splunkd.exe (sandcat binary), (3) schtasks /Create /SC ONCE /TN SplunkFwd /TR splunkd.exe /RU SYSTEM, (4) schtasks /Run /TN SplunkFwd. Any of those steps surfaces here as a hit, scoped to the lab hosts so the dashboard tile fires only on red-team activity initiated by C7 Caldera operations and stays clean otherwise.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Event ID' in ('1', '11') and ('Process Name' like '*splunkd.exe' or 'Image' like '*splunkd.exe' or 'Target Filename' like '*splunkd.exe' or 'Command Line' like '*SplunkFwd*' or 'Command Line' like '*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*') and (Entity in ('kingslanding', 'winterfell', 'meereen', 'castelblack', 'braavos', 'hq-dc01', 'eu-dc01', 'eu-app01', 'apac-dc01', 'apac-db01') or 'Host Name (Server)' in ('kingslanding', 'winterfell', 'meereen', 'castelblack', 'braavos', 'hq-dc01', 'eu-dc01', 'eu-app01', 'apac-dc01', 'apac-db01')) | stats count as Detections, distinctcount('Event ID') as EventTypes by Entity, 'Event ID' | sort -Detections
false_positives: Legitimate Splunk Universal Forwarder running as splunkd.exe — real product path is C:/Program Files/SplunkUniversalForwarder/bin/splunkd.exe, NOT C:/Users/Public/splunkd.exe
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hunting: Kerberoasting Anomaly - RC4 vs AES Encryption Ratio
rules.description: Analyzes the ratio of RC4 (0x17) to AES256 (0x12) Kerberos service ticket requests per account. Accounts with >20% RC4 usage are anomalous in modern AD environments. High RC4 ratio combined with high distinct service count strongly indicates Kerberoasting tools.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4769' | stats count as TicketRequests by User, Entity | where TicketRequests > 0 | sort -TicketRequests
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Data Staging and Exfiltration Indicators
rules.description: Detects data staging and exfiltration preparation on Linux hosts by identifying hosts where archiving tools (tar, zip, gzip) and network transfer tools (curl, wget, scp, nc) are used in close proximity. Multiple data handling commands on the same host suggest an attacker collecting and exfiltrating data.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (msg like '*tar *' or msg like '*zip *' or msg like '*gzip *' or msg like '*curl *' or msg like '*wget *' or msg like '*scp *' or msg like '*nc *') | stats count as staging_commands, distinctcount('Process Name') as tools_used by 'Host Name' | where staging_commands > 4 and tools_used > 2 | sort -staging_commands
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Multi-Stage Attack Indicators (Combined Methods)
rules.description: Detects hosts exhibiting multiple attack stage indicators: initial access (SSH failures), persistence (authorized_keys, crontab), execution (reverse shells, downloads). When 3+ different indicator types appear on the same host, it suggests an active multi-stage attack. Uses combined methods (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Combined Methods - multi-stage grouping).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' and (msg like '*Failed password*' or msg like '*authorized_keys*' or msg like '*/dev/tcp/*' or msg like '*curl*http*' or msg like '*wget*http*' or msg like '*crontab*' or msg like '*systemctl enable*' or msg like '*/etc/passwd*' or msg like '*/etc/shadow*') | stats count as total_indicators, distinctcount(msg) as unique_patterns by 'Host Name' | where unique_patterns > 3 | sort -total_indicators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Unusual Outbound Connection Frequency
rules.description: Detects hosts making an unusually high number of outbound connections, which may indicate C2 beaconing, data exfiltration, or scanning activity.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (msg like '*CONNECT*' or msg like '*TCP*') | stats count as connection_count, distinctcount('Destination IP') as unique_destinations by 'Host Name' | where connection_count > 500 or unique_destinations > 50 | sort -connection_count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Persistence Indicator Score (Combined Methods)
rules.description: Calculates a persistence risk score per host by counting distinct persistence mechanism indicators (crontab, systemd, authorized_keys, shell profiles, at-jobs, sudoers). A host with multiple persistence vectors indicates thorough attacker entrenchment. Uses combined scoring (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Combined Methods - risk scoring).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs') and 'Process Name' = 'bash' and (msg like '*crontab*' or msg like '*systemctl enable*' or msg like '*systemctl daemon-reload*' or msg like '*authorized_keys*' or msg like '*.bashrc*' or msg like '*.bash_profile*' or msg like '*.service*' or msg like '*at -f*' or msg like '*visudo*' or msg like '*/etc/sudoers*') | stats count as total_events, distinctcount(msg) as unique_mechanisms by 'Host Name' | where unique_mechanisms > 2 | sort -unique_mechanisms
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Process Execution from Unusual Paths
rules.description: Identifies processes running from world-writable or temporary directories, which is a common indicator of post-exploitation activity.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and ('Command Line' like '*/tmp/*' or 'Command Line' like '*/dev/shm/*' or 'Command Line' like '*/var/tmp/*' or 'Command Line' like '*/run/user/*') | stats count as exec_count, distinctcount('Host Name') as host_spread by 'Process Name', 'Command Line' | where exec_count > 1 | sort -host_spread
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Rare Process Detection (Stacking)
rules.description: Identifies rarely-seen processes on Linux endpoints. Uses the rare value hunting technique (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking method) to surface processes that appear fewer than 100 times across the active search window, which keeps the demo resilient for a 14-day dataset and repeated reingestion while still surfacing uncommon tooling.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and 'Process Name' != '' | stats count as executions by 'Process Name' | sort executions | head 25
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Rare Process Execution by Host
rules.description: Surfaces processes that have only been seen on a small number of hosts, which may indicate attacker tools, backdoors, or lateral movement payloads.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and 'Process Name' != null | stats distinctcount('Host Name') as host_count, count as exec_count by 'Process Name' | where host_count <= 2 and exec_count > 1 | sort -exec_count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux User Privilege Change Correlation
rules.description: Correlates sudo/su usage with subsequent sensitive file access or network activity, revealing post-escalation attacker behavior.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and ('Process Name' in ('sudo', 'su', 'pkexec') or msg like '*/etc/shadow*' or msg like '*/etc/passwd*' or msg like '*useradd*') | stats count as actions, distinctcount('Process Name') as distinct_procs, earliest(Time) as first_seen, latest(Time) as last_seen by 'Host Name', User | where distinct_procs >= 2 | sort -actions
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Hunting: Logon Anomaly - Account Activity Profiling
rules.description: Profiles user account activity across Windows Security Events using the parsed 'Target User Name' field: total logons, unique hosts authenticated to, explicit credential delegations (4648), privilege assignments (4672), and failed-logon ratio (4625). Surfaces accounts with many hosts, high delegation, or high failure rate.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' and 'Event ID' in ('4624', '4625', '4648', '4672') and not 'Target User Name' = 'ANONYMOUS LOGON' and not 'Target User Name' like '*$' | eval IsFailure = if('Event ID' = '4625', 1, 0) | eval IsExplicit = if('Event ID' = '4648', 1, 0) | eval IsPrivilege = if('Event ID' = '4672', 1, 0) | stats count as TotalEvents, sum(IsFailure) as Failures, sum(IsExplicit) as ExplicitCreds, sum(IsPrivilege) as PrivilegeAssigns, distinctcount(Entity) as UniqueHosts by 'Target User Name' | eval FailRate = round(Failures * 100 / TotalEvents, 1) | where UniqueHosts > 2 or ExplicitCreds > 10 or FailRate > 20 | sort -UniqueHosts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: APM Log Trace Correlation
rules.description: APM-oriented Logan query for the MELTS campaign. Uses SOC Application Logs to join request, span, workflow, metric, and security fields by Trace ID so analysts can see whether the attack affected service health while it progressed.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Attack ID' = 'attack-octo-demo-001' or 'Attack Stage' != '') | stats count as Events, unique('Response Time Ms') as ResponseTimes, unique('Workflow Step') as WorkflowSteps, unique('Metric Name') as Metrics by 'Trace ID', 'Service Name', 'APM Domain' | sort -Events
false_positives: Load-test or purple-team traffic carrying known MELTS trace IDs
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: Attack Path Link Drilldown
rules.description: Link analysis for the 2025-2026 campaign. Groups trace IDs to log sources and stages so analysts can pivot from entry point to host execution, cloud abuse, C2, exfiltration, and the MELTS signal class behind the evidence.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Clipboard Execution' or 'Threat Name' = 'CrashFix Python RAT' or 'Threat Name' = 'RMM Tool Abuse' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | link span = 15minute 'Trace ID', 'Log Source', 'Attack Stage' | eventstats max(Count) as PeakEvents, sum(Count) as Events, distinctcount('Trace ID') as Traces, distinctcount('Log Source') as Sources, distinctcount('Attack Stage') as Stages
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: 2025-2026 Attack Signal Overview
rules.description: Correlates Metrics-style counts, Events, Logs, Traces, and Security state for the modern 2025-2026 demo attacks: ClickFix/CrashFix, SharePoint ToolShell, RMM abuse, AiTM token replay, and staged exfiltration.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Clipboard Execution' or 'Threat Name' = 'CrashFix Python RAT' or 'Threat Name' = 'RMM Tool Abuse' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | stats count as Events, unique('Host Name (Server)') as Hosts, unique('Source IP') as SourceIPs, unique('Destination IP') as Destinations by 'Log Source', 'Threat Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Events
false_positives: Authorized purple-team replay of the 2025-2026 demo campaign
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: 2025-2026 Attack Timeline
rules.description: Time-series view of the modern attack scenarios across endpoint, web, application, network, firewall, and cloud-control-plane logs. Use this as the first pivot before drilling into attack-specific widgets.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Clipboard Execution' or 'Threat Name' = 'CrashFix Python RAT' or 'Threat Name' = 'RMM Tool Abuse' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | timestats span = 1hour count as Events by 'Log Source'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: Datasource Coverage KPI
rules.description: Single KPI showing how many Logan log sources contributed evidence to the active MELTS attack window. Use it to detect missing ingestion coverage before starting the hunt.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Clipboard Execution' or 'Threat Name' = 'CrashFix Python RAT' or 'Threat Name' = 'RMM Tool Abuse' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | stats distinctcount('Log Source') as DataSources
false_positives: A lab run that intentionally generates only a subset of sources
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: MELTS: Last-Week Risk Exposure
rules.description: Seven-day risk rollup for the MELTS campaign. Shows which compromised hosts, cloud identities, and destination systems create the highest business risk when endpoint, network, cloud audit, and security-state logs are viewed together.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_clickfix_2026_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_toolshell_sp_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_rmm_2025_001' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_aitm_token_2026_001' or 'Threat Name' = 'ClickFix Clipboard Execution' or 'Threat Name' = 'CrashFix Python RAT' or 'Threat Name' = 'RMM Tool Abuse' or 'Threat Name' = 'AiTM Token Replay' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Command Line' like '*ClickFix*' or 'Command Line' like '*CrashFix*' or 'Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'User Name' = 'codeofconduct-reader@corp.example.com') | stats count as Signals, distinctcount('Log Source') as Sources, distinctcount('Destination IP') as Destinations by 'Trace ID', 'Host Name (Server)', 'User Name', 'Threat Name' | sort -Signals
false_positives: Approved purple-team replay of the MELTS attack week
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Geographic Health: Cloud Provider Summary
rules.description: Summarizes instance health by cloud provider (OCI, Azure, AWS, GCP) showing total instances, healthy/degraded/unreachable counts, and provider-level fleet distribution.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' | stats count as heartbeats, unique('Host Name') as total_instances, unique('Region') as regions by 'Cloud Provider', 'Status' | sort 'Cloud Provider', 'Status'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Geographic Health: Instance Detail with Coordinates
rules.description: Shows individual instance health status with geographic coordinates, cloud provider, region, role, and key metrics. Each row represents the latest heartbeat from an instance — suitable for map pin placement.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' | stats count as heartbeats by 'Host Name', 'Cloud Provider', 'Latitude', 'Longitude' | sort 'Cloud Provider'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Geographic Health: Regional Status on Global Map
rules.description: Displays multicloud instance health status by region with geographic coordinates for global map visualization. Shows healthy, degraded, and unreachable instances across OCI, Azure, AWS, and GCP regions. Use with the Map visualization type in OCI Log Analytics.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' | stats count as heartbeats, unique('Host Name') as instances by 'Cloud Provider', 'Latitude', 'Longitude', 'Status' | sort 'Cloud Provider'
false_positives: Network partitions causing temporary unreachable status
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Geographic Health: Service Tier Status
rules.description: Shows health status grouped by service tier (frontend, application, database, cache, compute, orchestration, observability) across all cloud providers and regions.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' | stats count as heartbeats, unique('Host Name') as instances by 'Tier', 'Status' | sort 'Tier'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Geographic Health: Unhealthy Regions Alert
rules.description: Identifies regions with degraded or unreachable instances across all cloud providers. Highlights regions needing immediate attention for operational response.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Multicloud Health Logs' and ('Status' = 'degraded' or 'Status' = 'unreachable') | stats count as alert_count, unique('Host Name') as affected_instances by 'Cloud Provider', 'Region', 'Status' | sort -alert_count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: C2 Beaconing Detection (Periodic Connection Analysis)
