rules.description: Detects command-and-control beaconing by identifying hosts making periodic outbound connections to the same destination. C2 implants typically beacon at regular intervals. Groups network connections by source-destination pair and counts occurrences — a high count to a single destination suggests automated beaconing rather than human browsing.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' and 'Destination Port' != 80 and 'Destination Port' != 443 | stats count as connection_count by 'Host Name (Server)', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port' | where connection_count > 12 | sort -connection_count
false_positives: Monitoring agents with periodic health checks
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI After-Hours IAM Activity (Time-Based Anomaly)
rules.description: Detects IAM configuration changes made outside normal business hours (before 06:00 or after 22:00 UTC). Identity changes at unusual hours may indicate a compromised account being used when legitimate users are not monitoring. Uses time-based anomaly detection (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Forecasting/Anomaly Detection - temporal patterns).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.*' | eval hour = toNumber(formatDate(Time, 'HH')) | where hour < 6 or hour > 22 | stats count as after_hours_changes by 'User Name', 'Event Type' | sort -after_hours_changes
false_positives: Scheduled automation running outside business hours
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI API Call Burst by User
rules.description: Detects users making an unusually high number of API calls in a short window, which may indicate automated enumeration or data exfiltration scripts.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' | stats count as api_calls by 'User Name', 'Event Type' | where api_calls > 100 | sort -api_calls
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Audit Failures
rules.description: Alert-ready aggregation of OCI Audit control-plane operations whose parsed Status is Failure. This is a field-backed approximation of the referenced Splunk message-text search: it preserves failed 4xx/5xx activity but does not independently classify throttling when the parser does not expose it as Failure.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and Status = 'Failure' | stats count as AuditFailures, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Event Type', 'User Name', Status | sort -AuditFailures
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Console Login Brute Force (Frequency Analysis)
rules.description: Detects brute force or credential stuffing against OCI Console by counting failed login attempts per user. Uses frequency analysis (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking method) to identify accounts with more than 3 failed attempts in the time window.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' and Status = 'Failure' | stats count as failed_attempts by 'User Name' | where failed_attempts > 3 | sort -failed_attempts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Cross-Compartment Activity Anomaly
rules.description: Identifies users operating across an unusual number of compartments, which may indicate lateral movement or reconnaissance after initial access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' | stats distinctcount('Compartment Name') as compartment_count, count as total_actions by 'User Name' | where compartment_count > 5 | sort -compartment_count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Failed Action Spike by Source IP
rules.description: Identifies source IPs with a high ratio of failed to successful API calls, which may indicate credential stuffing or permission enumeration.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' | eval is_fail = if(Status = 'Failure', 1, 0) | stats count as total, sum(is_fail) as failures by 'Source IP' | eval fail_rate = failures * 100 / total | where fail_rate > 50 and total > 10 | sort -fail_rate
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI IAM and Fusion Activity Correlation
rules.description: Correlates OCI IAM identity events with Fusion Apps sign-in/sign-out and ESS audit activity. Flags identities or source IPs seen in both OCI and Fusion during the search window, which may indicate account misuse or suspicious cross-platform identity activity.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.*' or 'Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.*' or 'Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.IdentitySignOn.*')) or 'Log Source' = 'Fusion Apps: Sign In - Sign Out Activity Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Fusion Apps: ESS Audit Logs' | eval actor = if('User Name' != '', 'User Name', if(userInternalName != '', userInternalName, if(userID.loginID != '', userID.loginID, if('Source IP' != '', 'Source IP', if('Client IP' != '', 'Client IP', if(ipAddress != '', ipAddress, clientIp)))))) | eval source_type = if('Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs', 'oci_iam', 'fusion') | where actor != '' | stats count as total_events, distinctcount(source_type) as source_type_count, unique('Log Source') as correlated_sources, earliest(time) as first_seen, latest(time) as last_seen by actor | where source_type_count = 2 and total_events > 1 | sort -total_events
false_positives: Planned identity administration during Fusion rollout or migration
Large scheduled provisioning jobs touching OCI IAM and Fusion identities
Shared break-glass accounts used by multiple administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI IAM Policy Changes
rules.description: Alert-ready aggregation of OCI IAM policy create, update, and delete events. The event selection reuses the existing portable OCI IAM Policy Modified Sigma rule and adds only the aggregation required by scheduled-search detection rules.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy') | stats count as PolicyChanges, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Event Type', 'User Name', 'Source IP' | sort -PolicyChanges
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI IAM Rapid Configuration Changes (Anomaly Detection)
rules.description: Detects users making a high volume of IAM changes in a short time window. A burst of identity changes (policy updates, user creation, group modifications) from a single principal may indicate account compromise or insider threat. Uses frequency analysis with threshold (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Forecasting/Anomaly Detection method).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.*' | stats count as iam_changes by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where iam_changes > 10 | sort -iam_changes
false_positives: Terraform or IaC applying bulk configuration
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Multiple Users from Same IP (Grouping)
rules.description: Detects a single IP address being used to authenticate as multiple different OCI users. This pattern may indicate credential stuffing, shared compromised infrastructure, or an attacker testing multiple stolen credentials from the same origin. Uses distinct count grouping (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Grouping method).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' | stats distinctcount('User Name') as unique_users, count as total_logins by 'Source IP' | where unique_users > 2 | sort -unique_users
false_positives: Corporate VPN or NAT where multiple users share an egress IP
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Object Storage Access from External Source
rules.description: Alert-ready aggregation of OCI Object Storage operations from non-RFC1918 IPv4 source addresses. This preserves the referenced Splunk alert's public-source evidence but omits Splunk iplocation country enrichment and does not claim that the address is new relative to a historical baseline.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.*' and 'Source IP' != null and not ('Source IP' like '10.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.16.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.17.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.18.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.19.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.20.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.21.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.22.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.23.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.24.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.25.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.26.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.27.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.28.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.29.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.30.*' or 'Source IP' like '172.31.*' or 'Source IP' like '192.168.*') | stats count as ExternalAccesses, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Source IP', 'User Name', 'Event Type' | sort -ExternalAccesses
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Off-Hours Administrative Activity
rules.description: Surfaces administrative API calls occurring outside business hours (evenings, weekends), which may indicate unauthorized access or compromised accounts.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like '*create*' or 'Event Type' like '*delete*' or 'Event Type' like '*update*') | eval hour = formatDate(Time, 'HH') | eval day = formatDate(Time, 'E') | where hour in ('00', '01', '02', '03', '04', '05', '22', '23') or day = 'Sat' or day = 'Sun' | stats count as actions by 'User Name', day, hour | sort -actions
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Privilege Escalation Chain Detection
rules.description: Detects potential privilege escalation by identifying users who perform a sequence of IAM operations: creating policies, groups, or dynamic groups followed by adding themselves to privileged groups. Combines multiple identity control plane events from the same principal to surface escalation chains.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' like 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.*' | stats count as iam_ops, distinctcount('Event Type') as unique_actions by 'User Name' | where iam_ops > 5 and unique_actions > 3 | sort -iam_ops
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Programmatic Credential Creation Burst
rules.description: Correlates OCI Audit events for uploaded API keys, auth tokens, and customer secret keys. Multiple credential types or repeated creations by the same principal and source IP in one hunt window warrant review because they expand programmatic access paths.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.uploadapikey' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createauthtoken' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createcustomersecretkey') | stats count as CredentialChanges, distinctcount('Event Type') as CredentialTypes, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where CredentialChanges > 1 or CredentialTypes > 1 | sort -CredentialChanges
false_positives: Planned service-account onboarding or migration activity
Automation that rotates multiple credential types together
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Resource Deletion Wave
rules.description: Detects mass resource deletion patterns where multiple resources are deleted in rapid succession, indicating potential ransomware, sabotage, or account compromise.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like '*delete*' or 'Event Type' like '*terminate*') and Status = 'Success' | stats count as deletions, distinctcount('Resource Type') as resource_types by 'User Name' | where deletions > 10 | sort -deletions
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Resource Destruction Spike (Anomaly Detection)
rules.description: Identifies principals performing an abnormally high number of destructive operations (delete, terminate). A spike in resource destruction from a single user may indicate a compromised account performing sabotage, ransomware-style destruction, or an insider threat. Uses threshold-based anomaly detection (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Forecasting/Anomaly Detection method).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Event Type' like '*delete*' or 'Event Type' like '*terminate*' or 'Event Type' like '*remove*') | stats count as destructive_actions, distinctcount('Event Type') as unique_action_types by 'User Name', 'Source IP' | where destructive_actions > 5 | sort -destructive_actions
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Unusual API Caller - First Seen User-Agent
rules.description: Identifies API calls from user-agents that have not been seen in the baseline period, which may indicate new tooling or unauthorized API access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' | stats earliest(Time) as first_seen, count as call_count by 'User Agent' | where call_count < 5 | sort -first_seen
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI VCN: External Egress Traffic
rules.description: Shows accepted VCN flow records whose destination is outside private, loopback, link-local, and multicast IPv4 ranges. Use this baseline to review internet-bound traffic, then pivot by source, destination, port, flow count, and sampled byte values. This query intentionally scopes to outbound traffic; it does not classify private endpoints reached through a public address or IPv6 traffic.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' and 'Action' = 'ACCEPT' and 'Destination IP' != null and not ('Destination IP' like '10.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.16.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.17.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.18.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.19.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.20.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.21.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.22.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.23.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.24.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.25.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.26.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.27.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.28.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.29.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.30.*' or 'Destination IP' like '172.31.*' or 'Destination IP' like '192.168.*' or 'Destination IP' like '127.*' or 'Destination IP' like '169.254.*' or 'Destination IP' like '224.*' or 'Destination IP' like '225.*' or 'Destination IP' like '226.*' or 'Destination IP' like '227.*' or 'Destination IP' like '228.*' or 'Destination IP' like '229.*' or 'Destination IP' like '230.*' or 'Destination IP' like '231.*' or 'Destination IP' like '232.*' or 'Destination IP' like '233.*' or 'Destination IP' like '234.*' or 'Destination IP' like '235.*' or 'Destination IP' like '236.*' or 'Destination IP' like '237.*' or 'Destination IP' like '238.*' or 'Destination IP' like '239.*') | stats count as Flows, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSentSamples, unique('Bytes Received') as BytesReceivedSamples, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port', Protocol | sort -Flows | head 100
false_positives: Approved SaaS, software updates, OCI public endpoints, and internet-facing application dependencies
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI VCN Rejected Traffic Spike
rules.description: Alert-ready aggregation for a source address producing more than 100 rejected VCN flow records in the ten-minute scheduled-search window. This preserves the threshold behavior of the referenced Splunk alert while using OCI Log Analytics display fields.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' and 'Action' = 'REJECT' | stats count as RejectedFlows, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Source IP' | where RejectedFlows > 100 | sort -RejectedFlows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Octo Chaos — Stale Scenario State
rules.description: Identifies chaos-audit events where a scenario remains active past its TTL. Used by the chaos-cleanup playbook (tier: low) to auto-clear the registry.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' and Event = 'chaos.apply' | stats latest('Chaos Scenario') as scenario, latest('Chaos TTL Seconds') as ttl, count as applies by 'Chaos Target' | sort -applies
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Octo Checkout — DB Slowness Correlated With Chaos
rules.description: Surfaces p95 DB latency spikes on the Octo checkout workflow and splits them by whether a chaos scenario was active. Used by the coordinator db-slow-remediation playbook.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' and 'Workflow ID' = 'checkout' | eval is5xx = if('HTTP Status Code' >= 500, 1, 0) | eval ischaos = if('Chaos Injected' = 'true', 1, 0) | stats avg('DB Elapsed ms') as avg_db_ms, sum(is5xx) as errors, sum(ischaos) as chaos_events by Service | sort -avg_db_ms
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Octo WAF Detections vs App 5xx
rules.description: Joins OCI WAF detection events with Shop/CRM 5xx responses using the shared X-Request-Id header. Used to build the Security Posture dashboard and to feed the waf-tighten-suggest playbook.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs') and ('WAF Action' != null or 'HTTP Status Code' >= 500) | eval haswaf = if('WAF Action' != null, 1, 0) | eval is5xx = if('HTTP Status Code' >= 500, 1, 0) | stats count as events, sum(haswaf) as waf, sum(is5xx) as app5xx by 'Client IP', 'URL Path' | where waf > 0 and app5xx > 0 | sort -events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: RMM: Post-Compromise Remote Access Activity
rules.description: Detects remote monitoring and management tooling used after compromise, including ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, and Atera process execution plus outbound relay traffic.
rules.oci_query: (('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs') and ('Process Name' like '*ScreenConnect*' or 'Process Name' like '*AnyDesk*' or 'Process Name' like '*AteraAgent*' or 'Command Line' like '*screenconnect*' or 'Command Line' like '*anydesk*' or 'Command Line' like '*atera*')) or (('Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs') and ('Destination Hostname' like '*screenconnect*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*atera*' or 'Destination Hostname' like '*rmm*')) | stats count as Events, unique('Destination Hostname') as Destinations, unique('Command Line') as Commands by 'Host Name (Server)', 'Process Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SharePoint ToolShell: Exploitation Attempts
rules.description: Detects SharePoint ToolShell-style exploitation by looking for ToolPane and spinstall0.aspx activity across WAF, load balancer, web application, and application trace telemetry.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Request URL' like '*ToolPane.aspx*' or 'Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Attack Type' like '*ToolShell*' or 'Span Attributes' like '*ToolShell*') | stats count as Attempts, unique('Response Code') as ResponseCodes, unique('HTTP Method') as Methods by 'Log Source', 'Client IP', 'Request URL', 'Trace ID' | sort -Attempts
false_positives: SharePoint patch validation against a lab host
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SharePoint ToolShell: Webshell Post-Exploit
rules.description: Finds post-exploitation command attempts against SharePoint webshell paths, especially spinstall0.aspx command execution, backend 500s, and high-severity application spans.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Request URL' like '*spinstall0.aspx*' or 'Request URL' like '*cmd=*' or 'Attack Type' like '*ToolShell_webshell*' or 'Span Attributes' like '*webshell*') | stats count as Events, unique('Attack Type') as AttackTypes, unique('Response Code') as ResponseCodes by 'Log Source', 'Client IP', 'Request URL', 'Trace ID' | sort -Events
false_positives: Incident-response reproduction in a quarantined lab
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SSH Brute Force Detection (Frequency Analysis)
rules.description: Identifies SSH brute force attacks by counting failed login attempts per source IP. Uses frequency analysis (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking method) to surface IPs with more than 5 failed attempts, indicating automated credential guessing.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and msg like '*Failed password*' | stats count as failed_attempts by 'Client IP' | where failed_attempts > 5 | sort -failed_attempts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 1: External Port Scan, WAF/API Gateway 401/403 Bursts & VCN Flow Sweeps
rules.description: Detects Day 1 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: external reconnaissance and API enumeration bursts (HTTP 401/403 spikes) against shop and crm endpoints alongside anomalous inbound VCN Flow Log REJECT port sweeps from 198.51.100.214.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs') and ('Client IP' = '198.51.100.214' or 'Source IP' = '198.51.100.214' or 'Response Code' in ('401', '403') or 'Action' = 'REJECT') | stats count as recon_events, distinctcount('Destination Port') as ports_probed, distinctcount('Request URL') as urls_probed by 'Log Source', 'Trace ID' | where recon_events >= 1 | sort -recon_events
false_positives: Authorized external vulnerability assessment or scheduled DAST scanning windows
Public Internet background noise against perimeter load balancers
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 2: OKE Pod Breakout & IMDSv2 Credential Harvesting
rules.description: Detects Day 2 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: a compromised OKE application pod executing curl against the OCI Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254/opc/v2/instance/) and enumerating Kubernetes service account tokens.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Command Line' like '*169.254.169.254/opc/v2/instance/*' or 'Process Command Line' like '*169.254.169.254/opc/v2/instance/*' or msg like '*serviceaccount/token*') | stats count as breakout_hits, distinctcount('Process Name') as processes by 'Host Name', 'Process Name' | sort -breakout_hits
false_positives: OCI Kubernetes node initialization scripts calling IMDSv2 from the host namespace rather than an application pod
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 3: Caldera Agent Deployment & GOAD Active Directory Discovery
rules.description: Detects Day 3 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: Caldera Sandcat agent deployment (splunkd.exe) on GOAD-DC01 (kingslanding), GOAD-DC02 (winterfell), and GOAD-SRV02 (castelblack) followed by AdFind LDAP enumeration and SharpHound BloodHound collection.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Host Name (Server)' in ('kingslanding', 'winterfell', 'castelblack') or Entity in ('kingslanding', 'winterfell', 'castelblack')) and ('Command Line' like '*splunkd.exe*' or 'Command Line' like '*AdFind*' or 'Command Line' like '*SharpHound*') | stats count as discovery_events, distinctcount('Process Name') as tools_observed by 'Host Name (Server)', 'Process Name' | sort -discovery_events
false_positives: Legitimate Splunk Universal Forwarder binaries installed under C:\Program Files\SplunkUniversalForwarder\bin\
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 4: Living-off-the-Land RMM Tunnel, AMSI Bypass & Kerberoasting
rules.description: Detects Day 4 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: PowerShell encoded command execution and AMSI bypass attempts (EventID 4104), RMM tunnel creation (cloudflared.exe), and Kerberoasting RC4 ticket requests (EventID 4769) across GOAD servers.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows PowerShell Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Event ID' in ('4104', '4769', '1') and ('Command Line' like '*-EncodedCommand*' or 'Command Line' like '*cloudflared*' or 'Event ID' = '4769')) | stats count as lateral_events, distinctcount('Event ID') as distinct_signals by 'Host Name (Server)', 'Event ID' | sort -lateral_events
false_positives: Approved Cloudflare Tunnel connectors on designated edge gateway hosts
Legacy Active Directory service accounts explicitly configured for RC4 encryption
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 5: DCSync Replication & Service Persistence on GOAD KingsLanding
rules.description: Detects Day 5 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: Active Directory DCSync replication rights abuse (EventID 4662 DS-Replication-Get-Changes) on GOAD-DC01 (kingslanding) paired with Windows service installation persistence (EventID 7045 / 4698).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event System Logs') and ('Event ID' in ('4662', '7045', '4698') and 'Host Name (Server)' in ('kingslanding', 'winterfell', 'castelblack')) | stats count as persistence_events, distinctcount('Event ID') as event_types by 'Host Name (Server)', User | sort -persistence_events
false_positives: Legitimate Domain Controller computer accounts (ending in $) performing Active Directory replication
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 6: Oracle Data Safe & Autonomous Database Sensitive SQL Extraction
rules.description: Detects Day 6 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: unauthorized SQL schema enumeration (all_tab_columns) and bulk sensitive PII extraction (CRM_CORE.CUSTOMER_PII) against Autonomous Databases guardian-standalone-adb and oci4cca-observeai-adb.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' and ('DB Target' in ('guardian-standalone-adb', 'oci4cca-observeai-adb') or 'DB Statement' like '*CUSTOMER_PII*' or 'DB Statement' like '*all_tab_columns*') | stats count as db_audit_hits, distinctcount('DB Target') as targeted_databases by 'DB Target', User, 'Attack Stage' | sort -db_audit_hits
false_positives: Scheduled DBA schema migration or Oracle Data Safe sensitive data discovery job
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Storyline Day 7: DNS Tunneling, C2 Egress & ObserveAI MELTS Automated Containment
rules.description: Detects Day 7 of the 7-day multi-pillar adversary storyline: high-volume DNS tunneling queries (*.exfil.c2-stage.example.net) and outbound VCN Flow Log transfer to C2 IP 198.51.100.214, correlated across MELTS by the ObserveAI / Coordinator AI Agent.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Destination IP' = '198.51.100.214' or 'Client IP' = '198.51.100.214' or msg like '*exfil.c2-stage.example.net*') | stats count as exfil_signals, distinctcount('Log Source') as correlated_pillars by 'Destination IP', 'Trace ID' | sort -exfil_signals
false_positives: Approved external backup or CDN replication endpoints
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Login Activity Time-Series Anomaly
rules.description: Detects anomalous spikes in authentication activity using time-bucketed analysis. Groups login events into hourly buckets and flags hours with significantly more activity than the baseline. Uses timecluster-style analysis to identify burst authentication patterns that may indicate credential stuffing or compromised account usage.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' | timestats span = 1hour count as login_count | where login_count > 20
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: WAF Attack Frequency by Source IP (Frequency Analysis)
rules.description: Identifies source IPs generating the most WAF block events. Uses frequency analysis (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking) to surface prolific attackers targeting the web application. IPs with high block counts indicate automated attack tools.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI WAF Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs') and 'Action' = 'BLOCK' | stats count as blocked_requests, unique('Rule Key') as rules_triggered, earliest(time) as first_seen, latest(time) as last_seen by 'Client IP' | where blocked_requests > 10 | sort -blocked_requests
false_positives: WAF tuning generating false positive blocks
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: WAF Multi-Attack Vector Scoring (Combined Methods)
rules.description: Calculates a threat score per source IP based on the diversity of attack types (SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, command injection, SSRF). An IP triggering multiple different CRS rule categories indicates a sophisticated attacker using multiple techniques. Uses combined scoring (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Combined Methods).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI WAF Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs') and 'Action' = 'BLOCK' | stats count as total_blocks, distinctcount('Rule Key') as unique_rules, distinctcount('Rule Type') as attack_types, distinctcount('Request URL') as unique_urls by 'Client IP' | eval threat_score = total_blocks + (unique_rules * 5) + (attack_types * 10) | where unique_rules > 2 | sort -threat_score
false_positives: Authorized penetration testers running full OWASP scans
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SQL Injection Pattern Stacking (Rare Value Detection)
rules.description: Stacks unique SQL injection payloads observed in WAF events to identify attack tool signatures and novel injection techniques. Rare payloads may indicate custom exploits or new attack vectors. Uses rare value stacking (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI WAF Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs') and ('Request URL' like '*SELECT*' or 'Request URL' like '*UNION*' or 'Request URL' like '*OR 1=1*' or 'Request URL' like '*DROP*' or 'Request URL' like '*INSERT*' or 'Request URL' like '*--*' or 'Rule Key' like '*941*' or 'Rule Key' like '*942*' or Message like '*UNION*' or msg like '*UNION*') | stats count as occurrences by 'Request URL', 'Client IP' | sort -occurrences
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: File Integrity Monitoring Events
rules.description: FIM/syscheck changes (added/modified/deleted) by path and agent.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'FIM Event' != null | stats count as Count by 'Host Name', 'FIM Event', 'File Path' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Alert Level Distribution
rules.description: Distribution of all Wazuh alerts by rule level (severity).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' | stats count as Count by 'Wazuh Rule Level' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Recent Alerts (All)
rules.description: Threat-hunting explorer: most recent Wazuh alerts across all GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' | stats count as Events by 'Host Name', 'Wazuh Rule ID', 'Rule Description', 'Wazuh Rule Level' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Top Firing Rules
rules.description: Most frequently firing Wazuh rules across GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' | stats count as Count by 'Wazuh Rule ID', 'Rule Description' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: System Inventory
rules.description: Hardware and OS inventory per GOAD agent (cores, memory, CPU, OS).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Inventory' | stats count as Records by 'Host Name', 'CPU Name', 'OS Name' | sort -Records
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Installed Packages
rules.description: Installed software inventory across GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Inventory' and 'Package Name' != null | stats count as Count by 'Package Name' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Alerts Evolution Over Time
rules.description: Wazuh MITRE alert volume bucketed by tactic for the trend view.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Tactic' != null | stats count as Count by 'MITRE Tactic' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: MITRE Attacks by Technique
rules.description: Wazuh alert count grouped by MITRE ATT&CK technique id.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Technique ID' != null | stats count as Count by 'MITRE Technique ID', 'MITRE Technique' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Recent MITRE Events
rules.description: Most recent MITRE-mapped Wazuh alerts with technique, tactic, level and rule.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Technique ID' != null | stats count as Events by 'MITRE Technique ID', 'MITRE Tactic', 'Rule Description' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Rule Level by Tactic
rules.description: Wazuh alert severity (rule level) distribution per MITRE tactic.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Tactic' != null | stats count as Count by 'MITRE Tactic', 'Wazuh Rule Level' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Top Agents by MITRE Alerts
rules.description: GOAD agents ranked by number of MITRE-mapped Wazuh alerts.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Technique ID' != null | stats count as Count by 'Host Name' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Top MITRE Tactics
rules.description: Wazuh alert count grouped by MITRE ATT&CK tactic.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Tactic' != null | stats count as Count by 'MITRE Tactic' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: MITRE Detections (KPI)
rules.description: Total Wazuh alerts mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique across GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Alerts' and 'MITRE Technique ID' != null | stats count as Detections
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Compliance Mapping
rules.description: Failed SCA checks grouped by compliance framework (CIS/PCI).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh SCA' and 'SCA Check Result' = 'failed' | stats count as Count by 'SCA Compliance' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Failed SCA Checks
rules.description: Configuration checks that failed, by title and host.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh SCA' and 'SCA Check Result' = 'failed' | stats count as Count by 'Host Name', 'SCA Check Title' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: SCA Policy Score
rules.description: Security Configuration Assessment score per policy and agent.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh SCA' | stats count as Checks by 'Host Name', 'SCA Policy', 'SCA Score' | sort -Checks
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Vulnerabilities by Agent
rules.description: CVE count per GOAD agent.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' | stats count as Count by 'Host Name' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Critical Vulnerabilities (KPI)
rules.description: Count of Critical-severity CVEs detected by Wazuh on GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' and 'Vulnerability Severity' = 'Critical' | stats count as Critical
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: CVSS Score Distribution
rules.description: Distribution of detected CVEs by CVSS base score.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' | stats count as Count by 'CVSS Score' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: High Vulnerabilities (KPI)
rules.description: Count of High-severity CVEs detected by Wazuh.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' and 'Vulnerability Severity' = 'High' | stats count as High
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Low Vulnerabilities (KPI)
rules.description: Count of Low-severity CVEs detected by Wazuh.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' and 'Vulnerability Severity' = 'Low' | stats count as Low
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Medium Vulnerabilities (KPI)
rules.description: Count of Medium-severity CVEs detected by Wazuh.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' and 'Vulnerability Severity' = 'Medium' | stats count as Medium
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Top CVEs
rules.description: Most frequently detected CVEs across GOAD agents.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' | stats count as Count by 'CVE ID', 'Vulnerability Severity' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Wazuh: Top Vulnerable Packages
rules.description: Packages with the most associated CVEs.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Wazuh Vulnerabilities' | stats count as Count by 'Package Name' | sort -Count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web Attack Geographic Anomaly (Rare Country Detection)
rules.description: Identifies attack traffic originating from unusual countries by stacking WAF events by country code. Rare countries with high attack volumes may indicate targeted campaigns from specific threat actor regions.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI WAF Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs') and 'Action' = 'BLOCK' | stats count as attacks, unique('Client IP') as unique_ips by 'Country Code' | where attacks > 5 | sort -attacks
false_positives: VPN traffic from unusual exit nodes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web Application Brute Force Detection (Frequency Analysis)
rules.description: Identifies IPs performing brute force attacks against web login endpoints by counting 401/403 responses. Uses frequency analysis (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking) to surface credential stuffing and brute force campaigns.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and ('Response Code' = '401' or 'Response Code' = '403') and ('Request URL' like '*login*' or 'Request URL' like '*auth*' or 'Request URL' like '*signin*') | stats count as failed_attempts, unique('Request URL') as targeted_endpoints by 'Client IP' | where failed_attempts > 10 | sort -failed_attempts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web Directory Scanning IP Clustering (Anomaly Detection)
rules.description: Clusters IPs performing directory enumeration by counting distinct 404-generating paths. A high number of unique 404 paths from a single IP indicates systematic directory/file scanning using tools like dirb, gobuster, or ffuf.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and 'Response Code' = '404' | stats count as total_404s, distinctcount('Request URL') as unique_paths by 'Client IP', 'User Agent' | where unique_paths > 20 | sort -unique_paths
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OWASP Multi-Stage Web Attack Chain (Combined Methods)
rules.description: Correlates web attack indicators across WAF, Load Balancer, and application logs to identify multi-stage attack chains. An IP that triggers WAF blocks, generates auth failures, and accesses sensitive endpoints is likely executing a coordinated attack campaign. Uses combined methods (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Combined Methods - multi-stage grouping).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI WAF Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs') | stats count as total_events, distinctcount('Log Source') as log_sources, unique('Action') as actions, unique('Response Code') as status_codes by 'Client IP' | where log_sources > 1 | sort -total_events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web Scanner Tool Identification (User Agent Stacking)
rules.description: Stacks user agents across all web traffic to identify automated scanning tools, attack frameworks, and bot traffic. Non-browser user agents generating high request volumes from a small set of source IPs indicate active reconnaissance or automated exploitation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') | stats count as requests, distinctcount('Client IP') as source_ips, distinctcount('Response Code') as status_codes by 'User Agent' | where requests > 50 and source_ips < 5 | sort -requests
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Attack Path Link Analysis
rules.description: Link analysis groups all events carrying the web-to-cloud Trace ID or C2/object-storage pivots into a single path. Use this widget to drill from WAF entry to app host, network egress, firewall alert, and OCI Audit object access.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Client IP' = '203.0.113.50' or 'Source IP' = '10.0.1.50' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'User Name' = 'compromised-svc@corp.example.com' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration') | link span = 15minute 'Trace ID', 'Log Source' | eventstats max(Count) as PeakEvents, sum(Count) as Events, distinctcount('Trace ID') as Traces, distinctcount('Log Source') as Sources
false_positives: Red team replay of the demo chain
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Correlated Attack Timeline
rules.description: Summarizes the web-to-cloud attack chain across WAF, load balancer, application, host, VCN Flow, Network Firewall, Sysmon network, and OCI Audit logs. The shared Trace ID and fixed attacker/C2 pivots let analysts follow entry point, credential access, C2, cloud abuse, and exfiltration in one widget.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Client IP' = '203.0.113.50' or 'Source IP' = '10.0.1.50' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'User Name' = 'compromised-svc@corp.example.com' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration') | stats count as Events, unique('Request URL') as Requests, unique('Destination IP') as Destinations by 'Log Source', 'Trace ID' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: OCI Audit Cloud Abuse
rules.description: Filters OCI Audit for cloud discovery and Object Storage actions associated with the compromised service identity and web-to-cloud Trace ID.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'User Name' = 'compromised-svc@corp.example.com' or 'Resource Name' like '*prod-customer-backups*') | stats count as AuditEvents, unique('Event Type') as EventTypes, unique('Resource Name') as Resources by 'User Name', 'Source IP', Status | sort -AuditEvents
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Compromised Cloud Identity
rules.description: Highlights OCI Audit activity performed by the compromised service identity after instance metadata access. The widget surfaces Object Storage enumeration, object reads, and pre-authenticated request creation.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ('User Name' = 'compromised-svc@corp.example.com' or 'Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001') | stats count as CloudActions, distinctcount('Event Type') as UniqueActions, unique('Event Type') as EventTypes, unique('Resource Name') as Resources by 'User Name', 'Source IP', 'Trace ID' | sort -CloudActions
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Compromised Machines
rules.description: Shows hosts and private IPs tied to the compromise, including application host activity, Windows C2 telemetry, VCN flows, and firewall sessions. Analysts can pivot from host names to network tuples and command lines.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Host Name' = 'app-prod-02' or 'Host Name (Server)' = 'SRV01.sevenkingdoms.local' or 'Source IP' = '10.0.1.50' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77') | stats count as Events, unique('Process Name') as Processes, unique('Destination IP') as Destinations by 'Log Source', 'Host Name', 'Host Name (Server)', 'Source IP' | sort -Events
false_positives: Load testing from controlled security hosts
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Entry Point and SSRF Evidence
rules.description: Identifies the initial web request that reached the application tier and attempted access to the cloud instance metadata endpoint. Use the Request URL, Client IP, backend host, and Trace ID to start the investigation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs') and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Client IP' = '203.0.113.50' or 'Request URL' like '*169.254.169.254*') | stats count as Events, unique('Action') as Actions, unique('Response Code') as ResponseCodes, unique('Request URL') as Requests by 'Client IP', 'Trace ID', 'Log Source', 'Host Name' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Exfiltrated Data Evidence
rules.description: Combines application export messages, VCN Flow egress, Network Firewall threat alerts, and OCI Audit object reads to show what data left the environment and which destination received it.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs') and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration' or 'Resource Name' like '*customer-export-2026-05.csv*') | stats count as Evidence, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSent, unique('Resource Name') as Resources, unique('Threat Name') as Threats by 'Log Source', 'Destination IP', 'User Name', 'Trace ID' | sort -Evidence
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: Network Firewall C2 and Threat Alerts
rules.description: Correlates Network Firewall traffic and threat records for the C2 destination. Threat Name, Firewall Rule, byte counts, and action values show whether the exfiltration was alerted, allowed, or denied.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs' and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'Threat Name' != null) | stats count as Events, unique('Threat Name') as Threats, unique('Firewall Rule') as Rules, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSent by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Action', 'Log Type' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: MITRE Stage Breakdown
rules.description: Sunburst-friendly rollup of the web-to-cloud chain by evidence source and threat label. It shows whether evidence is present across initial access, host, network, firewall, and cloud-control-plane telemetry.
rules.oci_query: ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Client IP' = '203.0.113.50' or 'Source IP' = '10.0.1.50' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77' or 'User Name' = 'compromised-svc@corp.example.com' or 'Threat Name' = 'Suspicious Data Exfiltration') | stats count as Events by 'Log Source', 'Threat Name' | sort -Events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Web-to-Cloud: VCN Egress and Exfil Flows
rules.description: Surfaces accepted VCN Flow Log records from the compromised application host to the C2/exfil destination and OCI service endpoints. Large Bytes Sent values provide the primary network indicator for data loss.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC VCN Flow Logs' and ('Trace ID' = 'trace_w2c_entry_001' or 'Source IP' = '10.0.1.50' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.77') | stats count as Flows, unique('Action') as Actions, unique('Bytes Sent') as BytesSent, unique('Flow ID') as FlowIds by 'Source IP', 'Destination IP', 'Destination Port', 'Trace ID' | sort -Flows
false_positives: Approved bulk export from application subnet
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows High-Entropy DNS Queries
rules.description: Surfaces DNS queries with unusually long or high-entropy domain names, which are characteristic of DNS tunneling, DGA malware, or data exfiltration over DNS.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Query Name' != null | eval domain_length = length('Query Name') | stats count as query_count, avg(domain_length) as avg_length, max(domain_length) as max_length by 'Host Name' | where avg_length > 40 or max_length > 60 | sort -avg_length
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Lateral Movement Timeline
rules.description: Correlates SMB connections, remote service creation, and WinRM sessions to build a timeline of lateral movement activity across the environment.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Process Name' in ('psexec.exe', 'psexesvc.exe', 'winrs.exe', 'winrm.cmd') or 'Destination Port' in (445, 5985, 5986, 3389) or 'Pipe Name' like '*PSEXEC*') | stats count as events, distinctcount('Destination IP') as targets, earliest(Time) as start_time, latest(Time) as end_time by 'Host Name', User | where targets >= 2 | sort -targets
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows LOLBin Usage Frequency Anomaly
rules.description: Identifies hosts with abnormally high usage of living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), which may indicate fileless malware or attacker tool usage.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Process Name' in ('certutil.exe', 'mshta.exe', 'regsvr32.exe', 'rundll32.exe', 'wscript.exe', 'cscript.exe', 'msbuild.exe', 'bitsadmin.exe', 'wmic.exe', 'installutil.exe') | stats count as lolbin_count, distinctcount('Process Name') as distinct_lolbins by 'Host Name' | where lolbin_count > 20 or distinct_lolbins >= 4 | sort -lolbin_count
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Rare Parent-Child Process Relationships
rules.description: Identifies unusual parent-child process pairs that deviate from normal system behavior. Rare combinations may indicate process injection, living-off-the-land, or malware execution.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and 'Process Name' != null and 'Parent Process Name' != null | stats count as occurrence, distinctcount('Host Name') as host_count by 'Parent Process Name', 'Process Name' | where occurrence <= 3 and host_count <= 2 | sort occurrence
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Administrator Logon
rules.description: Alert-ready search for successful logons by the built-in Administrator account. Extend the approved-account filter for renamed or localized administrator accounts.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4624' and ('Target User Name' = 'Administrator' or User = 'Administrator') | stats count as AdministratorLogons, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Target User Name', 'Logon Type', 'Host Name (Server)' | sort -AdministratorLogons
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Failed Logon Burst by Source
rules.description: Alert-ready search for more than 10 Security Event 4625 failures from one source address in the five-minute scheduled-search window.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4625' | stats count as FailedLogons, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Source Address', 'Target User Name', 'Host Name (Server)' | where FailedLogons > 10 | sort -FailedLogons
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows New Local User Created
rules.description: Alert-ready search for Security Event 4720, indicating that a user account was created on a monitored Windows host.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4720' | stats count as UsersCreated, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Target User Name', 'Subject User Name', 'Host Name (Server)' | sort -UsersCreated
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows User Added to Administrators or Remote Desktop Users
rules.description: Alert-ready search for Security Event 4732 additions to the local Administrators or Remote Desktop Users groups.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4732' and ('Target User Name' like '*Administrators*' or 'Target User Name' like '*Remote Desktop Users*' or msg like '*Administrators*' or msg like '*Remote Desktop Users*') | stats count as GroupAdds, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by User, 'Target User Name', 'Host Name (Server)' | sort -GroupAdds
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Successful RDP Logon Outside Business Hours
rules.description: Alert-ready search for successful RemoteInteractive logons (Security Event 4624, logon type 10) outside the configured 08:00-18:00 query timezone.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and 'Event ID' = '4624' and 'Logon Type' = '10' | eval hour = toNumber(formatDate(Time, 'HH')) | where hour < 8 or hour >= 18 | stats count as RDPLogons, earliest(Time) as FirstSeen, latest(Time) as LastSeen by 'Target User Name', 'Source Address', 'Host Name (Server)' | sort -RDPLogons
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Credential Access Tool Cluster (Grouping)
rules.description: Groups credential access tool indicators by host and user to identify active credential harvesting campaigns. When multiple credential dumping techniques (Mimikatz, LSASS access, Kerberoasting, NTDS.dit) appear on the same host, it indicates systematic credential theft. Uses grouping (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Grouping method).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and (('Command Line' like '*sekurlsa*') or ('Command Line' like '*lsass*') or ('Command Line' like '*mimikatz*') or ('Command Line' like '*procdump*lsass*') or ('Command Line' like '*comsvcs*MiniDump*') or ('Command Line' like '*kerberoast*') or ('Command Line' like '*ntds*') or ('Command Line' like '*WDigest*')) | stats count as cred_events, distinctcount('Command Line') as unique_techniques by 'Host Name', User | sort -cred_events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Defense Evasion Score (Combined Methods)
rules.description: Calculates a defense evasion risk score per host by counting distinct evasion indicators: event log clearing, AMSI bypass, firewall modification, UAC bypass, process hollowing. Hosts exhibiting multiple evasion techniques indicate sophisticated attackers actively disabling security controls. Uses combined scoring (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Combined Methods - risk scoring).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and (('Command Line' like '*wevtutil*cl*') or ('Command Line' like '*Clear-EventLog*') or ('Command Line' like '*AmsiUtils*') or ('Command Line' like '*amsiInitFailed*') or ('Command Line' like '*netsh*firewall*') or ('Command Line' like '*advfirewall*set*off*') or ('Command Line' like '*fodhelper*') or ('Command Line' like '*eventvwr*') or ('Command Line' like '*NtUnmapViewOfSection*') or ('Command Line' like '*CREATE_SUSPENDED*')) | stats count as evasion_events, distinctcount('Command Line') as unique_techniques by 'Host Name' | where unique_techniques > 1 | sort -unique_techniques
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Lateral Movement Tool Cluster (Grouping)
rules.description: Groups lateral movement tool usage by host to identify systems being used as pivot points. When multiple lateral movement tools (PsExec, RDP, WinRM, remote shares) appear on the same host, it strongly suggests active lateral movement. Uses grouping/clustering (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Grouping method).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and (('Process Name' like '*psexec*') or ('Process Name' like '*mstsc*') or ('Command Line' like '*Enter-PSSession*') or ('Command Line' like '*Invoke-Command*') or ('Command Line' like '*wmic*node*')) | stats count as lateral_events, distinctcount('Process Name') as unique_tools by 'Host Name' | where unique_tools > 1 | sort -lateral_events
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Suspiciously Long Command Line (Field Analysis)
rules.description: Flags processes with unusually long command lines (>500 chars). Attackers frequently use long command lines for encoded payloads, obfuscated scripts, and base64-encoded commands. Uses eval-based field creation (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Searching/Filtering method with field creation).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' | eval cmd_len = length('Command Line') | where cmd_len > 500 | sort -cmd_len | fields 'Process Name', 'Command Line', cmd_len, 'Host Name', User
false_positives: Legitimate PowerShell scripts with many parameters
Deployment tools with long argument lists
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Process from Unusual Path (Rare Value Analysis)
rules.description: Identifies processes executing from non-standard paths commonly used by attackers (Temp, Public, AppData, Downloads). Legitimate software typically runs from Program Files or System32. Uses rare path analysis (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking + Field Analysis).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and (('Process Name' like '*Temp*') or ('Process Name' like '*Users*Public*') or ('Process Name' like '*AppData*Local*Temp*') or ('Process Name' like '*Downloads*') or ('Process Name' like '*ProgramData*')) | stats count as executions by 'Process Name', 'Host Name' | sort -executions
false_positives: Temp files created by legitimate updaters
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Windows Rare Process Detection (Stacking)
rules.description: Identifies rarely-seen processes on Windows endpoints. Uses the rare value hunting technique (Threat Hunter's Cookbook: Sorting/Stacking method) to surface processes that appear fewer than 80 times across the active search window, which keeps the demo resilient for a 14-day dataset and repeated reingestion while still highlighting uncommon attacker tooling.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and 'Process Name' != '' | stats count as executions by 'Process Name' | sort executions | head 25
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Image File Execution Options Debugger
rules.description: Detects setting of Image File Execution Options debugger for persistence or tampering.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Image File Execution Options*' and 'Command Line' like '*Debugger*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Impacket atexec Remote Scheduled Task Execution
rules.description: Detects impacket atexec, which creates a transient scheduled task on a remote host (via the ATSvc/Task Scheduler) to run a command and redirect output to an admin share. Indicators: a task launched by the Task Scheduler running cmd with output redirected to ADMIN$/a temp marker file.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Parent Process Name' like '*svchost.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*taskeng.exe')) and (('Command Line' like '*cmd.exe*' and 'Command Line' like '*2>&1*')) and (('Command Line' like '*ADMIN$*' or 'Command Line' like '*Temp*' or 'Command Line' like '*2>&1*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Impacket wmiexec Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects impacket wmiexec-style remote execution, where commands run via WMI (Win32_Process Create) with output redirected to a local admin share, e.g. 'cmd.exe /Q /c <cmd> 1> \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__<ts> 2>&1'. A classic semi-interactive lateral-movement pattern.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (( ('Parent Process Name' like '*WmiPrvSE.exe') and (('Command Line' like '*1>*' or 'Command Line' like '*2>&1*' or 'Command Line' like '*1>*')) ) or (('Command Line' like '*cmd.exe*' and 'Command Line' like '*ADMIN$*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Indirect Command Execution via Forfiles
rules.description: Detects usage of forfiles.exe for indirect command execution to bypass application controls.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\forfiles.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*/c*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Insecure Deserialization Attack Detected
rules.description: Detects insecure deserialization attacks where malicious serialized objects are sent to achieve remote code execution. OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs') and ((('Attack Type' = 'deserialization' or 'Attack Type' = 'insecure_deserialization' or 'Attack Type' = 'object_injection')) or ('OWASP Category' like '*Integrity*') or (('Request Body' like '*rO0AB*' or 'Request Body' like '*java.lang.Runtime*' or 'Request Body' like '*java.lang.ProcessBuilder*' or 'Request Body' like '*ysoserial*' or 'Request Body' like '*ObjectInputStream*' or 'Request Body' like '*__reduce__*' or 'Request Body' like '*pickle.loads*' or 'Request Body' like '*yaml.load*' or 'Request Body' like '*unserialize(*' or 'Request Body' like '*O:4:"User"*')))
false_positives: Legitimate serialized data in API payloads
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference Detected
rules.description: Detects IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) attacks where users access resources belonging to other users by manipulating object IDs in URLs. OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs') and (('Attack Type' = 'IDOR') or ('OWASP Category' like '*Broken Access Control*'))
false_positives: Admin users legitimately accessing other user profiles
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: InstallUtil Application Whitelisting Bypass
rules.description: Detects usage of InstallUtil.exe to execute code through .NET assemblies, bypassing application controls.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\InstallUtil.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*/U*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Internal Monologue NTLM Hash Theft
rules.description: Detects Internal Monologue attack which retrieves NTLM hashes without touching LSASS.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*InternalMonologue*' or 'Command Line' like '*internal_monologue*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: JavaScript Execution via Node.js
rules.description: Detects Node.js executing inline JavaScript or scripts from suspicious locations.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\node.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*-e *' or 'Command Line' like '*--eval*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Kerberoasting: RC4 Encrypted Service Ticket Request
rules.description: Detects Kerberos service ticket requests (Event 4769) using RC4 encryption (TicketEncryptionType 0x17) which is a strong indicator of Kerberoasting. Modern AD environments use AES256 (0x12) by default; RC4 requests are anomalous and typically indicate tools like Rubeus, Invoke-Kerberoast, or GetUserSPNs.py extracting service ticket hashes for offline cracking.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4769') and ('Ticket Encryption Type' = '0x17') and not ('Service Name' like '*$')) | stats count as Requests by User | sort -Requests
false_positives: Legacy applications requiring RC4 Kerberos tickets
Misconfigured service accounts with RC4 only
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Kerberoasting: SPN Sweep - Multiple Service Tickets from Single Account
rules.description: Detects a single account requesting service tickets for multiple distinct services in a short window, indicating SPN sweep for offline hash cracking. Rubeus kerberoast and Invoke-Kerberoast request tickets for all SPN-enabled accounts rapidly. Normal users request 1-3 service tickets; attackers request 10+.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4769')) | stats count as TotalRequests by User, Entity | where TotalRequests > 10 | sort -TotalRequests
false_positives: Service accounts legitimately accessing many services
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Kerberos Ticket Export via Mimikatz
rules.description: Detects Kerberos ticket exporting commands used in pass-the-ticket and golden ticket attacks.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*kerberos::list*' or 'Command Line' like '*kerberos::ptt*' or 'Command Line' like '*export*' or 'Command Line' like '*.kirbi*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Keylogging via PowerShell Get-Keystrokes
rules.description: Detects PowerShell-based keylogging techniques using API hooks or input monitoring.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Get-Keystrokes*' or 'Command Line' like '*SetWindowsHookEx*' or 'Command Line' like '*GetAsyncKeyState*' or 'Command Line' like '*keylog*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: LAPS Clear-Text Local Admin Password Read Attempt
rules.description: Detects attempts to read the LAPS-managed local administrator password from the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd attribute. Tooling includes LAPSToolkit, Get-AdmPwdPassword, and pyLAPS. GOAD includes a LAPS reader path to recover local admin passwords.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-AdmPwdPassword*' or 'Command Line' like '*LAPSToolkit*' or 'Command Line' like '*pyLAPS*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-LAPSADPassword*')))
false_positives: LAPS administrative password retrieval by helpdesk
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Lateral Movement: Account Authenticating from Multiple Sources
rules.description: Detects a single account performing network logons (LogonType 3) from 3+ distinct source IPs — indicates lateral movement sweep or compromised credential reuse.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4624' and 'Logon Type' = '3') and not (('Target User Name' = 'ANONYMOUS LOGON' or 'Target User Name' = '-')) and not ('Target User Name' like '*$')) | stats distinctcount('Source Address') as UniqueSources, count as TotalLogons by User, Entity | where UniqueSources > 3 | sort -UniqueSources
false_positives: Domain admin accounts from multiple workstations
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Lateral Tool Transfer via Robocopy
rules.description: Detects usage of robocopy to transfer tools or files to remote systems.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\robocopy.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*\\\\*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: LaZagne Credential Harvester
rules.description: Detects execution of LaZagne, an open-source credential harvesting tool that extracts passwords from multiple applications.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*lazagne*' or 'Command Line' like '*LaZagne*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Archive Data Collected for Exfiltration
rules.description: Detects creation of compressed archives from sensitive directories. Attackers archive collected data (credentials, source code, configs) before exfiltrating to reduce transfer size and avoid detection.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs') and 'Process Name' = 'bash' and ((msg like '*tar*' or msg like '*zip*') and (msg like '*/etc/*' or msg like '*/home/*' or msg like '*/root/*' or msg like '*/var/www/*' or msg like '*/opt/*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux At Job Scheduled
rules.description: Detects scheduling of at jobs for deferred command execution. Attackers use at jobs for timed persistence or delayed payload execution.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (('Process Name' = 'at') or ('Process Name' = 'batch'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Bind Shell Listener
rules.description: Detects creation of bind shell listeners using netcat, socat, or ncat. Bind shells open a listening port that allows remote attackers to connect and execute commands.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*nc -lvp*' or msg like '*nc -lp*' or msg like '*ncat -lvp*' or msg like '*ncat -lp*' or msg like '*netcat -lvp*')) or (msg like '*socat TCP-LISTEN*'))
false_positives: Network troubleshooting using netcat in listen mode
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Boopkit eBPF Rootkit Activity
rules.description: Detects boopkit/eBPF rootkit activity including BPF program/map loading, XDP attachment, and magic-packet triggered command execution. Boopkit hides reverse shells via eBPF and is invoked by attacker-crafted SYN packets.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and ((msg like '*boopkit*') or (msg like '*bpftool prog load*' or msg like '*bpftool map create*' or msg like '*bpftool prog show pinned*') or (msg like '*/sys/fs/bpf/*') or (msg like '*XDP_REDIRECT*') or (msg like '*magic packet*' and msg like '*reverse shell*'))
false_positives: Authorized eBPF observability tooling (bpftool, bcc, bpftrace) used by SREs
Cilium/Calico CNI bpf program loads on Kubernetes worker nodes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Container Escape Attempt
rules.description: Detects patterns indicating container escape attempts including access to Docker socket, cgroup manipulation, or nsenter usage from within containers.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*nsenter -t 1 -m -u -i -n -p*' or msg like '*/var/run/docker.sock*' or msg like '*mount -t cgroup*' or msg like '*release_agent*' or msg like '*core_pattern*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Crontab Modification
rules.description: Detects crontab command execution, which may indicate persistence via scheduled tasks.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (('Process Name' = 'crontab') and (('Command Line' like '*-e*' or 'Command Line' like '*-r*' or 'Command Line' like '*/tmp/*' or 'Command Line' like '*/var/tmp/*' or 'Command Line' like '*/dev/shm/*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Cryptominer Activity Detected
rules.description: Detects execution of known cryptomining software or command patterns associated with unauthorized cryptocurrency mining on compromised hosts.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*xmrig*' or msg like '*minerd*' or msg like '*cpuminer*' or msg like '*stratum+tcp*' or msg like '*stratum+ssl*' or msg like '*cryptonight*' or msg like '*--donate-level*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux DNS Tunneling Detected
rules.description: Detects execution of DNS tunneling tools such as iodine, dns2tcp, or dnscat2 used to exfiltrate data or establish covert C2 channels over DNS.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*iodine*' or msg like '*dns2tcp*' or msg like '*dnscat*' or msg like '*dnscrypt-proxy*' or msg like '*dnsmasq --server*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Encrypted Channel C2 Communication
rules.description: Detects establishment of encrypted communication channels that may indicate C2 activity. Attackers use OpenSSL, stunnel, and encrypted reverse shells to establish covert command and control over TLS/SSL.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*openssl s_client -connect*' or msg like '*openssl s_server*')) or ((msg like '*stunnel*' or msg like '*stunnel.conf*')) or ((msg like '*ncat --ssl*' or msg like '*socat openssl-connect*' or msg like '*socat OPENSSL*')) or ((msg like '*ssh -R*' or msg like '*ssh -fNR*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
rules.description: Detects data exfiltration using non-standard protocols. Attackers use tools like netcat, socat, or raw sockets to send data over TCP/UDP to external hosts, bypassing HTTP/HTTPS-based monitoring.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs') and 'Process Name' = 'bash' and (((msg like '*nc -w*' or msg like '*nc -q*' or msg like '*ncat --send*' or msg like '*socat - TCP*' or msg like '*socat STDIN TCP*')) or ((msg like '*| nc *' or msg like '*| ncat *' or msg like '*| socat *' or msg like '*| curl -X POST*')) or ((msg like '*scp -r /*' or msg like '*scp /etc*' or msg like '*scp /var/log*' or msg like '*scp /home*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux External Remote Service Abuse
rules.description: Detects suspicious use of external remote services (SSH, VPN, RDP via xfreerdp) from unusual or unauthorized sources. Attackers abuse external-facing remote services with stolen or default credentials to gain initial access.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (('Process Name' = 'sshd' and msg like '*Accepted*') or ((msg like '*openvpn*' or msg like '*wireguard*' or msg like '*strongswan*')) or ((msg like '*xfreerdp*' or msg like '*rdesktop*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Hidden File or Directory Creation in Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects creation of hidden files or directories (starting with dot) in world-writable or suspicious locations commonly used by attackers to stash tools and payloads.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*/tmp/.*' or msg like '*/var/tmp/.*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/.*' or msg like '*/run/lock/.*')))
false_positives: Applications creating hidden temporary configuration files
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux History File Cleared
rules.description: Detects clearing of command history files or unsetting of history environment variable, a common anti-forensics technique.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and ((msg like '*unset HISTFILE*') or (msg like '*history -c*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Hosts File Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of /etc/hosts or /etc/resolv.conf. Attackers modify these to redirect traffic, bypass security controls, or perform DNS hijacking.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (((msg like '*/etc/hosts*' or msg like '*/etc/resolv.conf*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux Kernel Module Loaded from Temp Directory
rules.description: Detects loading of kernel modules from temporary directories (/tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp), a strong indicator of rootkit installation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Secure Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Syslog Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Linux Audit Logs') and (('Process Name' = 'insmod' and (msg like '*/tmp/*' or msg like '*/dev/shm/*' or msg like '*/var/tmp/*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Linux LD_PRELOAD Library Hijacking
