rules.name: OCI API Key Uploaded
rules.description: Detects upload of a new API key to a user account.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.uploadapikey'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Audit Configuration Changed
rules.description: Detects modifications to OCI Audit service configuration including retention period changes. Reducing audit retention is a defense evasion tactic.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.audit.updateconfiguration'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Audit Configuration Retention Reduced
rules.description: Detects changes to audit configuration that may shorten retention period to destroy evidence.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.audit.updateconfiguration') and ('Original Log Content' like '*retentionPeriodDays*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Auth Token Created
rules.description: Detects creation of auth tokens (SWIFT passwords) which provide programmatic access to OCI Object Storage and Container Registry. Could indicate credential staging for data exfiltration.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createauthtoken'))
false_positives: Authorized Docker registry or API access setup
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Autonomous Database Terminated
rules.description: Detects termination of an OCI Autonomous Database, which may indicate sabotage or unauthorized resource destruction.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.databaseservice.deleteautonomousdatabase'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Bastion Session Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a Bastion session providing SSH or port-forwarding access to private resources. Unusual bastion sessions may indicate lateral movement.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.bastion.createsession'))
false_positives: Routine administrative access to private subnets
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Boot Volume Backup Created by Non-Admin
rules.description: Detects boot volume backup creation which could be used to copy instance data for exfiltration.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.computeapi.createbootvolumebackup'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
rules.description: Detects excessive cloud infrastructure enumeration via OCI API calls. Attackers with compromised credentials perform reconnaissance by listing instances, networks, buckets, and databases to map the cloud environment.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.computeapi.listinstances' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.listvcns' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.listsubnets' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.listbuckets' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.listusers' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.listgroups' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.listpolicies' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.databaseservice.listautonomousdatabases')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Cloud Shell Session Started
rules.description: Detects OCI Cloud Shell session activation. Cloud Shell provides authenticated CLI access to the tenancy and can be used for reconnaissance, data access, or lateral movement.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.cloudshell.startenvironment' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.cloudshell.createenvironment')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Compartment Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of an OCI compartment. This is a high-impact destructive action that removes all resources within the compartment and could indicate sabotage or insider threat.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletecompartment'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Compute Instance Terminated
rules.description: Detects successful termination of a compute instance, indicating potential resource destruction or evidence tampering.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.computeapi.terminateinstance' and (Status = 'Success' or Status = '200')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Console Login Failure
rules.description: Detects failed console login attempts to OCI, which may indicate brute-force or credential stuffing attacks.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' and Status = 'Failure'))
false_positives: Users with expired passwords or MFA issues
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Console Login from Suspicious IP Range
rules.description: Detects console login events that may indicate unauthorized access from unusual sources.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.interactivelogin'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Console Login from Unusual IP
rules.description: Detects a successful login to the OCI Console from an IP address not typically associated with the user.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' and (Status = 'Success' or Status = '200')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Cross-Region Data Copy
rules.description: Detects cross-region copy operations for boot volumes, block volumes, or object storage buckets. This could indicate data staging for exfiltration to a region outside organizational control.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.blockvolumes.copybootvolumeregion' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.blockvolumes.copyvolumeregion' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.copyobject' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createreplicationpolicy')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Customer Secret Key Created
rules.description: Detects creation of customer secret keys (S3-compatible access keys) for OCI Object Storage. These keys provide direct API access and may be used for data exfiltration.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createcustomersecretkey'))
false_positives: Migration tools requiring Object Storage access
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Database Backup Exported
rules.description: Detects database backup creation that could be used to extract sensitive data.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.databaseservice.createbackup'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Database System Terminated
rules.description: Detects termination of OCI Database Systems (BaseDB, Exadata). Unauthorized database termination can result in critical data loss and service disruption.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.databaseservice.terminatedbsystem' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.databaseservice.deletedbhome')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI DRG Attachment Created
rules.description: Detects creation of Dynamic Routing Gateway attachment, enabling network connectivity between VCNs or on-premises.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrgattachment'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Dynamic Group Created
rules.description: Detects creation of dynamic groups which grant instance principal permissions. Attackers can abuse this for lateral movement from compromised compute instances.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createdynamicgroup'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Dynamic Group Created with Broad Matching
rules.description: Detects creation of dynamic groups with instance principal matching that may grant excessive permissions.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createdynamicgroup') and (('Original Log Content' like '*Any {*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*compartment.id*' or 'Original Log Content' like '*instance.compartment.id*')))
false_positives: Legitimate dynamic group creation for instance principals
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Federated Identity Provider Modified
rules.description: Detects modification of SAML/OIDC identity provider configuration which could enable unauthorized access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidentityprovider' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidentityprovider')))
false_positives: Federation configuration changes by IAM admins
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Function Invoked
rules.description: Detects invocation of OCI Functions (serverless). Function invocations should be monitored as they can execute arbitrary code with the function's resource principal permissions.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.functions.invokefunction'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI IAM Admin Policy Created with Manage All
rules.description: Detects creation of an IAM policy containing overly permissive 'manage all-resources' statement, which grants full administrative access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy' and 'Original Log Content' like '*manage all-resources*') or ('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy' and 'Resource Name' like '*manage all-resources*'))
false_positives: Routine policy changes by authorized administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI IAM Policy Modified
rules.description: Detects changes to OCI IAM Policies.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy')))
false_positives: Routine policy changes by authorized administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Identity Provider Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a new identity provider (SAML/OIDC federation), which could indicate an attacker establishing persistent backdoor access via federated identity.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidentityprovider' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createsaml2identityprovider')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Instance Console Connection Created
rules.description: Detects creation of serial or VNC console connections to compute instances. Console connections bypass network controls and may indicate unauthorized access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.computeapi.createinstanceconsoleconnection'))
false_positives: Troubleshooting instances with network connectivity issues
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Instance Metadata Service Accessed
rules.description: Detects access to instance metadata service which may reveal instance principal credentials.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.computeapi.getinstancecredentials'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI KMS Key Scheduled for Deletion
rules.description: Detects scheduling an OCI Vault key for deletion. This can render encrypted data permanently inaccessible.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.kms.schedulekeydeletion'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI KMS Key Version Disabled
rules.description: Detects disabling of a KMS key version which may impact data encryption or indicate key compromise response.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.keymanagement.disablekeyversion'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Local Peering Gateway Created
rules.description: Detects creation of VCN local peering gateway enabling communication between VCNs within same region.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Log Archival Policy Disabled
rules.description: Detects modification of logging configuration that may reduce log retention or disable archival.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.logging.updatelog'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Log Group Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of OCI Log Analytics log groups. Deleting log groups destroys collected log data and can indicate an attacker covering their tracks.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.loganalytics.deleteloganalyticsloggroup' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.logging.deleteloggroup')))
false_positives: Log group consolidation during infrastructure cleanup
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI MFA Fatigue Attack Indicators
rules.description: Detects multiple MFA enrollment or verification attempts that may indicate MFA fatigue push attack.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatemfatotpdevice'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Network Firewall Policy Modified
rules.description: Detects modifications to OCI Network Firewall policies. Unauthorized changes could weaken network security posture or create bypass routes.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.networkfirewall.updatenetworkfirewallpolicy' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.networkfirewall.deletenetworkfirewall' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.networkfirewall.updatenetworkfirewall')))
false_positives: Routine policy changes by authorized administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Network Load Balancer Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of an OCI load balancer, which may cause service outages or indicate infrastructure sabotage.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.loadbalancer.deleteloadbalancer' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.networkloadbalancer.deletenetworkloadbalancer')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Network Security Group Rule Added for All Protocols
rules.description: Detects adding NSG rules that allow all protocols, potentially opening attack surface.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.addnetworksecuritygroupsecurityrules'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Network Security Group Updated
rules.description: Detects updates to Network Security Groups (NSGs).
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatenetworksecuritygroup' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.addnetworksecuritygroupsecurityrules')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Notification Subscription Created
rules.description: Detects creation of notification topic subscriptions. Attackers may create subscriptions to exfiltrate alerts or intercept security notifications.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.ons.createsubscription'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Object Storage Bucket Made Public
rules.description: Detects when a bucket's visibility is set to public.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.updatebucket' and 'Original Log Content' like '*"publicAccessType":"ObjectRead"*'))
false_positives: Routine storage operations by authorized administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Object Storage Pre-Authenticated Request Created
rules.description: Detects creation of pre-authenticated requests (PARs) for OCI Object Storage. PARs bypass IAM authentication and can be used for data exfiltration via shareable URLs.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createpreauthenticatedrequest'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Object Storage Replication Policy Created
rules.description: Detects creation of cross-region object storage replication policy, a potential data movement vector.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createreplicationpolicy'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Password Spraying Attack
rules.description: Detects password spraying by monitoring failed OCI Console login attempts across multiple user accounts. Unlike brute force (many attempts against one user), password spraying tries a few passwords against many accounts to avoid lockout thresholds.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.consolesignon.login' and Status = 'Failure')) | stats distinctcount('User Name') as distinct_users by 'Source IP' | where distinct_users > 5
false_positives: Employees with expired or rotated passwords
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Policy Allows Manage All Resources
rules.description: Detects update of existing IAM policies to include manage all-resources, an overprivileged access pattern that may indicate privilege escalation.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy' and 'Original Log Content' like '*manage all-resources*'))
false_positives: Emergency access policy creation by tenancy admins
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Route Table Update
rules.description: Detects changes to VCN Route Tables.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateroutetable' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable')))
false_positives: Network infrastructure changes during maintenance windows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Security List Allows All Protocols
rules.description: Detects security list updates that allow all protocols (protocol=all) from any source, creating an overly permissive network configuration that violates STIG network segmentation requirements.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist') and 'Original Log Content' like '*"protocol":"all"*'))
false_positives: Network infrastructure changes during maintenance windows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Service Gateway Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a service gateway that bypasses internet to access OCI services, a potential lateral movement path.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createservicegateway'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI User Capabilities Escalation
rules.description: Detects enabling console password for a user, potentially escalating a service account to interactive access.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createorupdateusercapabilities'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI User MFA Not Enabled
rules.description: Detects OCI user accounts where multi-factor authentication has been disabled or not configured, violating STIG requirement for strong authentication.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletemfatotpdevice' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletemfatotpdevice')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI User Password Reset by Admin
rules.description: Detects an administrator resetting another user's console password. This could indicate account takeover or unauthorized access provisioning.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createorupdateuiconsolepassword' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.resetuiconsolepassword')))
false_positives: Legitimate password resets by help desk
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Vault Key Rotation Overdue
rules.description: Detects disabling of key rotation schedule for OCI Vault encryption keys. Key rotation is a STIG requirement for cryptographic key management.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.kms.updatekeyversion'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Vault Secret Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of secrets from OCI Vault. Secret deletion can indicate an attacker covering tracks or disrupting application functionality.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.vault.schedulesecretdeletion' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.vault.deletesecret')))
false_positives: Routine secret rotation with scheduled deletion
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI Vault Secret Version Deprecated
rules.description: Detects deprecation of vault secret versions which may indicate secret rotation bypass.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.vaultsecret.deprecatesecretversion'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI VCN Flow Log Disabled
rules.description: Detects deletion or disabling of VCN flow logs which may indicate an attempt to hide network activity.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteflowlog'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI VCN Peering Connection Created
rules.description: Detects creation of VCN peering connections (local or remote). Unauthorized peering can extend network access across compartments or regions, enabling lateral movement.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createremotepeeringconnection' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.connectremotepeeringconnections')))
false_positives: Network infrastructure changes during maintenance windows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI VCN Security List Open to World
rules.description: Detects creation or update of a Security List allowing ingress from 0.0.0.0/0.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist') and 'HTTP Method' = 'POST' and 'Original Log Content' like '*0.0.0.0/0*'))
false_positives: Network infrastructure changes during maintenance windows
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI WAF Configuration Updated
rules.description: Detects changes to Web Application Firewall configurations.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and ((('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.waf.updatewebappfirewall' or 'Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.waf.updatewebappfirewallpolicy')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: OCI WAF Policy Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of Web Application Firewall policies which may expose applications to attacks.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'OCI Audit Logs' and (('Event Type' = 'com.oraclecloud.waf.deletewebappfirewallpolicy'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Office Application Startup Persistence
rules.description: Detects modification of Office startup locations for add-in persistence.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*\\Microsoft\\Word\\STARTUP*' or 'Command Line' like '*\\Microsoft\\Excel\\XLSTART*' or 'Command Line' like '*AddIns*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Overpass-the-Hash via Rubeus asktgt
rules.description: Detects overpass-the-hash (pass-the-key), where a stolen NTLM hash or AES key is used with Rubeus 'asktgt' to request a fresh TGT, converting an NTLM hash into full Kerberos access. Indicators: asktgt with /rc4, /aes256, or /des and a /user + /domain.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*asktgt*' and 'Command Line' like '*/user:*')) and (('Command Line' like '*/rc4:*' or 'Command Line' like '*/aes256:*' or 'Command Line' like '*/aes128:*' or 'Command Line' like '*/des:*' or 'Command Line' like '*/ntlm:*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Parent PID Spoofing
rules.description: Detects indicators of Parent PID spoofing, where a process fakes its parent for evasion.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS*' or 'Command Line' like '*ppid*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Pass-the-Cert / UnPAC-the-Hash via Certipy auth
rules.description: Detects authentication using a stolen or forged certificate (pass-the-cert) and PKINIT UnPAC-the-hash, where Certipy 'auth' is used with a .pfx to obtain a TGT and recover the account NT hash from the PAC. Rubeus asktgt with /getcredentials /certificate performs the equivalent.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (( (('Command Line' like '*certipy*' and 'Command Line' like '*auth*')) and (('Command Line' like '*-pfx*' or 'Command Line' like '*.pfx*')) ) or (('Command Line' like '*asktgt*' and 'Command Line' like '*/getcredentials*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Pass-the-Ticket via Rubeus
rules.description: Detects Rubeus commands for pass-the-ticket lateral movement using Kerberos tickets.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*rubeus*' or 'Command Line' like '*ptt*' or 'Command Line' like '*createnetonly*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Pass-the-Ticket: Excessive Explicit Credential Logons
rules.description: Detects Event 4648 explicit credential delegation at high frequency from a single source — indicates pass-the-ticket, over-pass-the-hash, or Rubeus asktgt lateral movement across the domain.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4648')) | stats count as Attempts by User, Entity | where Attempts > 5 | sort -Attempts
false_positives: Service accounts delegating credentials to multiple servers
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Password Policy Discovery
rules.description: Detects commands querying password policy settings, often part of pre-brute-force recon.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*net accounts*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Port Monitor DLL Persistence
rules.description: Detects registration of port monitor DLLs which run in the context of the Print Spooler service.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Monitors*' and 'Command Line' like '*Driver*' and 'Command Line' like '*reg*' and 'Command Line' like '*add*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Potato Privilege Escalation Tool
rules.description: Detects execution of various Potato family privilege escalation tools (JuicyPotato, SweetPotato, etc.).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*JuicyPotato*' or 'Command Line' like '*SweetPotato*' or 'Command Line' like '*RottenPotato*' or 'Command Line' like '*PrintSpoofer*' or 'Command Line' like '*GodPotato*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PowerShell Execution via Alternate Shell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell execution using alternate host processes (pwsh, powershell_ise) that may bypass logging.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Process Name' like '*\\pwsh.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\powershell_ise.exe')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PowerShell Script Block with Suspicious Keywords
rules.description: Detects PowerShell commands containing keywords commonly associated with offensive techniques.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*Invoke-Expression*' or 'Command Line' like '*IEX*' or 'Command Line' like '*Invoke-Command*' or 'Command Line' like '*New-Object Net.WebClient*' or 'Command Line' like '*DownloadString*' or 'Command Line' like '*DownloadFile*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PowerShell: Suspicious Command Execution (Real Windows Security Events)
rules.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell commands in Windows Security Event 4688 process creation logs. Covers download cradles, encoded execution, AMSI bypass, credential access, and common attack framework commands. Optimized for real Windows Security Events (not Sysmon) using Original Log Content matching.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and ('Event ID' = '4688') and ( (('Command Line' like '*invoke-webrequest*' or 'Command Line' like '*downloadstring*' or 'Command Line' like '*downloadfile*' or 'Command Line' like '*iwr *' or 'Command Line' like '*wget *' or 'Command Line' like '*curl *' or 'Command Line' like '*net.webclient*' or 'Command Line' like '*start-bitstransfer*')) or (('Command Line' like '*-enc*' or 'Command Line' like '*-encodedcommand*' or 'Command Line' like '*frombase64string*' or 'Command Line' like '*tobase64string*')) or (('Command Line' like '*amsiutils*' or 'Command Line' like '*amsiinitfailed*' or 'Command Line' like '*reflection.assembly*' or 'Command Line' like '*setvalue($null,$true)*')) or (('Command Line' like '*get-credential*' or 'Command Line' like '*mimikatz*' or 'Command Line' like '*sekurlsa*' or 'Command Line' like '*lsadump*' or 'Command Line' like '*invoke-mimikatz*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-gpppassword*' or 'Command Line' like '*find-localadminaccess*')) or (('Command Line' like '*get-domainuser*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-domaingroup*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-domaincomputer*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-netuser*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-netgroup*' or 'Command Line' like '*get-netcomputer*' or 'Command Line' like '*invoke-sharefinder*' or 'Command Line' like '*invoke-kerberoast*' or 'Command Line' like '*invoke-bloodhound*')) ) | stats count as Detections by 'Command Line' | sort -Detections
false_positives: IT automation scripts using encoded PowerShell
Security tools performing legitimate AD queries
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PowerView / PowerSploit Domain Reconnaissance
rules.description: Detects PowerView domain reconnaissance cmdlets used to enumerate users, groups, ACLs, trusts, and delegation across Active Directory. Heavily used in GOAD walkthroughs prior to privilege escalation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Get-DomainUser*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-DomainComputer*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-DomainGroup*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-NetUser*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-NetComputer*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-ObjectAcl*' or 'Command Line' like '*Find-InterestingDomainAcl*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-DomainTrust*' or 'Command Line' like '*Invoke-ACLScanner*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Print Processor Persistence
rules.description: Detects registration of malicious print processors for persistence via the Print Spooler service.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Print Processors*' and 'Command Line' like '*reg*' and 'Command Line' like '*add*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PrinterBug / SpoolSample Authentication Coercion
rules.description: Detects exploitation of the MS-RPRN PrinterBug (SpoolSample / printerbug.py) to coerce a target (often a DC) into authenticating to an attacker host. Used to relay or to capture a TGT from an unconstrained-delegation host. Distinct from the already-covered PetitPotam (MS-EFSRPC) coercion.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*SpoolSample*' or 'Command Line' like '*printerbug*' or 'Command Line' like '*dementor*' or 'Command Line' like '*RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification*' or 'Command Line' like '*MS-RPRN*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PrintNightmare Exploitation Attempt
rules.description: Detects exploitation of Print Spooler vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527) for privilege escalation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*AddPrinterDriverEx*' or 'Command Line' like '*PrintNightmare*' or 'Command Line' like '*SharpPrintNightmare*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Privilege Escalation: Sensitive Privileges Assigned to Non-Admin
rules.description: Detects Event 4672 with dangerous privileges (SeDebugPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege) assigned to non-SYSTEM accounts. Indicates token manipulation or privilege escalation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4672' and ('Privilege List' like '*SeDebugPrivilege*' or 'Privilege List' like '*SeTcbPrivilege*' or 'Privilege List' like '*SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege*' or 'Privilege List' like '*SeLoadDriverPrivilege*')) and not (('Subject User Name' = 'SYSTEM' or 'Subject User Name' = '-')) and not ('Subject User Name' like '*$')) | stats count as Assignments by User | sort -Assignments
false_positives: Service accounts with legitimate elevated privileges
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Process Discovery via Tasklist
rules.description: Detects tasklist.exe with verbose or SVC flags often used during post-exploitation reconnaissance.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\tasklist.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*/v*' or 'Command Line' like '*/svc*' or 'Command Line' like '*/fi*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Process Doppelganging via TxF
rules.description: Detects indicators of process doppelganging using transactional NTFS to replace process memory.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*NtCreateTransaction*' or 'Command Line' like '*NtRollbackTransaction*' or 'Command Line' like '*doppelganging*')))
false_positives: Development or debugging tools using TxF
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Process Ghosting or Herpaderping
rules.description: Detects indicators of process ghosting or herpaderping evasion techniques based on suspicious process creation patterns.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*NtCreateProcessEx*' or 'Command Line' like '*NtCreateSection*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Process Injection via CreateRemoteThread
rules.description: Detects suspicious processes commonly used as injection vehicles with command-line indicators of injection.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*VirtualAllocEx*' or 'Command Line' like '*WriteProcessMemory*' or 'Command Line' like '*CreateRemoteThread*' or 'Command Line' like '*NtMapViewOfSection*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PsExec-style Remote Service Installation (Event 7045)
rules.description: Detects creation of a Windows service (System Event 7045) whose binary path is a randomly named or admin-share executable, the on-host artifact of PsExec / impacket smbexec / paexec lateral movement. Pairs with the existing process-creation PsExec rules by catching the service-control-manager record.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '7045') and ( (('Service Name' like '*PSEXESVC*' or 'Service Name' like '*PAExec*' or 'Service Name' like '*RemCom*' or 'Service Name' like '*csexec*')) or (('Service File Name' like '*ADMIN$*' or 'Service File Name' like '*Temp*' or 'Service File Name' like '*system32*' or 'Service File Name' like '*.bat*')) ))
false_positives: Legitimate third-party service installs and software deployment agents
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: PsExec Service Installation
rules.description: Detects PsExec creating its service (PSEXESVC) on a remote machine.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*PSEXESVC*' or 'Command Line' like '*psexec*')))
false_positives: Legitimate PsExec usage by IT administrators
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Python Execution as Child of System Process
rules.description: Detects Python being executed as a child of system services or common LOLBins.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\python.exe' and ('Parent Process Name' like '*\\cmd.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\services.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\svchost.exe')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Query Registry for Security Products
rules.description: Detects registry queries checking for installed security products.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\reg.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*AntiVirusProduct*' or 'Command Line' like '*FirewallProduct*' or 'Command Line' like '*SecurityCenter*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Ransomware File Extension Indicators
rules.description: Detects commands associated with ransomware encryption activities based on known file extension patterns.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*.encrypted*' or 'Command Line' like '*.locked*' or 'Command Line' like '*.crypted*' or 'Command Line' like '*.enc*' or 'Command Line' like '*.crypt*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: RBCD Configuration via PowerShell / PowerView
rules.description: Detects command-line configuration of Resource-Based Constrained Delegation by writing PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount or msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity with Set-ADComputer / PowerView Set-DomainObject. Often follows a computer-account creation (MachineAccountQuota).
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount*' or 'Command Line' like '*msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity*' or 'Command Line' like '*Set-ADComputer*' or 'Command Line' like '*Get-ADComputer*')) and (('Command Line' like '*AllowedToAct*' or 'Command Line' like '*DelegateTo*' or 'Command Line' like '*rbcd*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: RBCD: msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity Modified (Event 5136)
rules.description: Detects writes to the msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity attribute via Directory Service object modification (Event 5136), the core of a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) takeover. The schemaIDGUID 3f78c3e5-f79a-46bd-a0b8-9d18116ddc79 identifies the attribute. GOAD uses webdav+RBCD to take over computer objects.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '5136' and ('Properties' like '*3f78c3e5-f79a-46bd-a0b8-9d18116ddc79*' or 'Properties' like '*msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: RDP Session Hijacking via tscon
rules.description: Detects RDP session hijacking using tscon.exe to connect to disconnected sessions.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\tscon.exe'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Reflective DLL Loading Indicators
rules.description: Detects indicators of reflective DLL loading where DLLs are loaded from memory without touching disk.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*ReflectiveLoader*' or 'Command Line' like '*Invoke-ReflectivePEInjection*' or 'Command Line' like '*sRDI*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Registry Run Key Modification via Reg.exe
rules.description: Detects registry run key modifications using reg.exe for persistence.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\reg.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*add*' and 'Command Line' like '*CurrentVersion\\Run*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Regsvcs or Regasm Execution for Code Bypass
rules.description: Detects execution of Regsvcs.exe or Regasm.exe to register COM objects from untrusted locations.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Process Name' like '*\\RegSvcs.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\RegAsm.exe')) and not ('Command Line' like '*Microsoft.NET*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Remote Service Creation via SC
rules.description: Detects remote service creation using sc.exe with the \\hostname syntax.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\sc.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*\\\\*' and 'Command Line' like '*create*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Renamed System Binary Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of renamed system utilities where the original filename does not match the current image name.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Original File Name' = 'powershell.exe') and not (('Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\pwsh.exe')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Root Certificate Installation via Certutil
rules.description: Detects installation of root certificates which could enable MitM attacks or trust arbitrary code.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\certutil.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*-addstore*' and 'Command Line' like '*Root*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SAM Database Extraction via Reg Save
rules.description: Detects extraction of the SAM database using reg.exe save command, used to obtain password hashes offline.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\reg.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*save*' and 'Command Line' like '*sam*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Scheduled Task XML Import
rules.description: Detects importing scheduled tasks from XML files, which may bypass task creation monitoring.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\schtasks.exe' and ('Command Line' like '*/create*' and 'Command Line' like '*/xml*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Screen Capture via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell commands capturing screenshots using .NET classes.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*CopyFromScreen*' or 'Command Line' like '*Drawing.Bitmap*' or 'Command Line' like '*screenshot*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: ScreenSaver Hijacking Persistence
rules.description: Detects modification of screensaver registry settings for persistence.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*SCRNSAVE.EXE*' and 'Command Line' like '*reg*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Scripting Engine Spawning Network Utility
rules.description: Detects scripting engines spawning network utilities like curl, wget, or net.exe.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Parent Process Name' like '*\\wscript.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\cscript.exe' or 'Parent Process Name' like '*\\mshta.exe') and ('Process Name' like '*\\cmd.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\powershell.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\net.exe' or 'Process Name' like '*\\net1.exe')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SDelete Secure File Deletion
rules.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals SDelete for secure file deletion to destroy forensic evidence.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Process Name' like '*\\sdelete.exe'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Security Group Enumeration: Rapid Membership Queries
rules.description: Detects Event 4799 rapid security group membership enumeration — indicates BloodHound/SharpHound or net group /domain reconnaissance.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs') and (('Event ID' = '4799')) | stats count as Queries by User, Process, Entity | where Queries > 50 | sort -Queries
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Security Support Provider DLL Persistence
rules.description: Detects registration of Security Support Provider DLLs for credential interception.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*Security Packages*' and 'Command Line' like '*reg*' and 'Command Line' like '*add*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: SeDebugPrivilege Abuse
rules.description: Detects tools attempting to enable or abuse SeDebugPrivilege for process manipulation.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ((('Command Line' like '*SeDebugPrivilege*' or 'Command Line' like '*AdjustTokenPrivileges*' or 'Command Line' like '*privilege::debug*')))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Sensitive Data Endpoint Access
rules.description: Detects access to endpoints that may expose sensitive data (database exports, configuration files, backup files). OWASP A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures / A01 Broken Access Control.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'OCI Load Balancer Access Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and ((('Response Code' = '200' or 'Response Code' = '301' or 'Response Code' = '302')) and (('Request URL' like '*.sql*' or 'Request URL' like '*.bak*' or 'Request URL' like '*.old*' or 'Request URL' like '*.backup*' or 'Request URL' like '*.dump*' or 'Request URL' like '*.log*' or 'Request URL' like '*.conf*' or 'Request URL' like '*.cfg*' or 'Request URL' like '*.ini*' or 'Request URL' like '*.key*' or 'Request URL' like '*.pem*' or 'Request URL' like '*.cert*' or 'Request URL' like '*.p12*' or 'Request URL' like '*.jks*' or 'Request URL' like '*.env*' or 'Request URL' like '*.htpasswd*' or 'Request URL' like '*.htaccess*' or 'Request URL' like '*/debug/*' or 'Request URL' like '*/trace/*' or 'Request URL' like '*/dump/*' or 'Request URL' like '*phpinfo*')))
false_positives: Legitimate access to log viewing endpoints
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: 7-zip-prep-for-exfiltration
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, "Exchange Server zero-days exploited in the wild".
In early March 2021, Microsoft released patches for four different zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft Exchange Server. The vulnerabilities were being used in a coordinated attack. For more information on the vulnerabilities, visit the following links:
1. CVE-2021-26855
2. CVE-2021-26857
3. CVE-2021-26858
4. CVE-2021-27065
The following query detects 7-zip activity associated with this threat. 7-ZIP is a legitimate tool used for file archiving; however, unusual 7-ZIP activity combined with other evidence might indicate that an attacker is compressing data for exfiltration.
More queries related to this threat can be found under the See also section of this page.
Reference - https://msrc-blog.microsoft.com/2021/03/02/multiple-security-updates-released-for-exchange-server/
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Process Name' = '7z.exe') and ('Command Line' like '*ProgramData\\\\pst*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Acronis - Multiple Endpoints Accessing Malicious URLs
rules.description: Multiple endpoints accessing malicious URLs could indicate an ongoing phishing attack, with several employees interacting with those URLs.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Azure Common Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and (Provider = 'Acronis') and ('Event ID' = 'MaliciousUrlDetected') | stats count as MaliciousUrlDetected by 'Host Name (Server)'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Acronis - Multiple Endpoints Infected by Ransomware
rules.description: Detects when three or more distinct endpoints report ransomware detections within a single day.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Azure Common Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and (Provider = 'Acronis') and ('Event ID' = 'ActiveProtectionBlocksSuspiciousActivity') | stats count as ActiveProtectionBlocksSuspiciousActivity by 'Host Name (Server)'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Acronis - Multiple Inboxes with Malicious Content Detected
rules.description: Many inboxes containing malicious content could indicate a potential ongoing phishing attack.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Azure Common Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and (Provider = 'Acronis') and ('Event ID' in ('MaliciousURLDetectedInM365MailboxBackup', 'MalwareDetectedInM365MailboxBackup', 'MaliciousEmailDetectedPerceptionPointWarning')) | stats count as MaliciousContent by 'Host Name (Server)'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AcroRd-Exploits
rules.description: The following query look for suspicious behaviors observed by the samples analyzed in the report.
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and ('Parent Process Name' = 'acrord32.exe' and 'Target Filename' like '*\\\\Start Menu\\\\Programs\\\\Startup*') | fields 'Target Filename', 'Host Name (Server)', Time, 'Process Name', 'Command Line', Hashes
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: AD account with Don't Expire Password
rules.description:
'Identifies whenever a user account has the setting "Password Never Expires" in the user account properties selected.
This is indicated in Security event 4738 in the EventData item labeled UserAccountControl with an included value of %%2089.
%%2089 resolves to "Don't Expire Password - Enabled".'
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Event System Logs')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Add malicious user to Admins and RDP users group via PowerShell
rules.description: Look for adding a user to Administrators in remote desktop users via PowerShell.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Parent Process Name' = 'powershell.exe') and (('Command Line' like '*$admins=*' and 'Command Line' like '*System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier*' and 'Command Line' like '*Translate*' and 'Command Line' like '*-split*' and 'Command Line' like '*localgroup*' and 'Command Line' like '*/add*' and 'Command Line' like '*$rdp=*'))
references: https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/blob/63ff8eedc58e7df0d22eba05ca73c92b59a66634/Hunting Queries/Microsoft 365 Defender/Ransomware/DEV-0270/Add malicious user to Admins and RDP users group via PowerShell.yaml
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: alt-data-streams
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Ransomware continues to hit healthcare, critical services. There is also a related blog.
In April of 2020, security researchers observed multiple ransomware campaigns using the same set of techniques.
The following query detects suspicious use of Alternate Data Streams (ADS), which may indicate an attempt to mask malicious activity. These campaigns have been known to deploy ransomware in-memory and exploit ADS.
The See also section below lists more queries related to techniques shared by these campaigns.
References:
https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2020/04/28/ransomware-groups-continue-to-target-healthcare-critical-services-heres-how-to-reduce-risk/
https://docs.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/streams
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Command Line' like '-q -s*' and 'Command Line' like '-p*' and not(('Target Filename' like '*visual studio*' or 'Target Filename' like '*ide*'))) | timestats span = 1hour unique('Command Line') as set_ProcessCommandLine, unique('Target Filename') as set_FolderPath, unique('Command Line') as set_InitiatingProcessCommandLine by Entity
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Apache 2.4.49 flaw CVE-2021-41773
rules.description: 'Detects using Apache 2.4.49 flaw CVE-2021-41773'
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and ('HTTP Request Method' = 'GET') and (('Request URL' like '*/cgi-bin/*' and 'Request URL' like '*/%2e%2e/*')) and ('HTTP Status Code' = 200)
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Command in URI
rules.description: 'Detects command in URI'
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and (('Request URL' like '*whoami*' or 'Request URL' like '*dpkg*' or 'Request URL' like '*useradd*' or 'Request URL' like '*sudo*' or 'Request URL' like '*cat*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Known malicious user agent
rules.description: 'Detects known malicious user agents'
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and (('User Agent' like '*Metasploit*' or 'User Agent' like '*360Spider*' or 'User Agent' like '*404checker*' or 'User Agent' like '*AllSubmitter*' or 'User Agent' like '*BackDoorBot*' or 'User Agent' like '*CATExplorador*' or 'User Agent' like '*Nikto*' or 'User Agent' like '*havij*'))
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Multiple client errors from single IP
rules.description: 'Detects multiple client errors from one source in short timeframe'

rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Multiple server errors from single IP
rules.description: 'Detects multiple server errors from one source in short timeframe'

rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Apache - Unexpected Post Requests
rules.description: 'Query detects Unexpected Post Requests'
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC WAF Security Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Web Application Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Load Balancer Access Logs') and ('HTTP Request Method' in ('POST', 'PUT')) | fields 'Request URL', 'HTTP Status Code'
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: ApexOne - Attack Discovery Detection

rules.name: ApexOne - C&C callback events

rules.name: ApexOne - Multiple deny or terminate actions on single IP

rules.name: ApexOne - Top sources with alerts

rules.name: app-armor-stopped
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Sysrv botnet evolution.
Sysrv is a Go-based botnet that targets both Windows and Linux servers, and steals resources to mine cryptocurrency.
The following query finds instances of the attacker attempting to stop the AppArmor network security service on devices running Linux.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Command Line' like '*/bin/bash /tmp/*' and 'Command Line' like '*service apparmor stop*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Box - Executable file in folder

rules.name: c2-lookup-from-nonbrowser[Nobelium]
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Solorigate supply chain attack. Please note that these attacks are currently known as the Nobelium campaign.
Microsoft detects the 2020 SolarWinds supply chain attack implant and its other components as part of a campaign by the Nobelium activity group. Nobelium is the threat actor behind the attack against SolarWinds, which was previously referred to as Solorigate.
Nobelium silently added malicious code to legitimate software updates for Orion, which is IT monitoring software provided by SolarWinds. In this way, malicious dynamic link libraries (DLLs) were distributed to SolarWinds customers.
The following query detects events when Nobelium received a DNS response after launching a lookup request to known command-and-control infrastructure.
More Nobelium-related queries can be found listed under the See also section of this document.
References:
https://msrc-blog.microsoft.com/2020/12/13/customer-guidance-on-recent-nation-state-cyber-attacks/
https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2020/12/18/analyzing-solorigate-the-compromised-dll-file-that-started-a-sophisticated-cyberattack-and-how-microsoft-defender-helps-protect/
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (Action = 'DnsQueryResponse' and Properties like '*.avsvmcloud*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: check-for-shadowhammer-activity-download-domain
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, ShadowHammer supply chain attack
Operation ShadowHammer was an attack against ASUS computer hardware, using the company's own update infrastructure to deliver malware to the company's products. The campaign ran from June to November, 2018. ASUS has since responded with updates that protect their Live Update system, and diagnostic tools to check affected systems.
The following query checks for activity associated with the ShadowHammer download domain over the past 30 days.
References:
https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/pan9wn/hackers-hijacked-asus-software-updates-to-install-backdoors-on-thousands-of-computers
https://www.asus.com/News/hqfgVUyZ6uyAyJe1
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs') and ('Request URL' = 'asushotfix.com' or 'Destination IP' = '141.105.71.116')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: clear-system-logs
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Ransomware continues to hit healthcare, critical services. There is also a related blog.
In April of 2020, security researchers observed multiple ransomware campaigns using the same set of techniques.
The following query detects attempts to use fsutil.exe to clear system logs and delete forensic artifacts.
The See also section below lists more queries related to techniques shared by these campaigns.
Reference - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2020/04/28/ransomware-groups-continue-to-target-healthcare-critical-services-heres-how-to-reduce-risk/
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Process Name' = 'fsutil.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*usn*' and 'Command Line' like '*deletejournal*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Clear System Logs
rules.description: This hunting query searches for attempts to use fsutil.exe to clear system logs and delete forensic artifacts.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Process Name' = 'fsutil.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*usn*' and 'Command Line' like '*deletejournal*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: Clearing of forensic evidence from event logs using wevtutil
rules.description: This query checks for attempts to clear at least 10 log entries from event logs using wevtutil.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Command Line' like '*WEVTUTIL*' and 'Command Line' like '*CL*') | timestats span = 5minute distinctcount('Command Line') as LogClearCount, unique('Command Line') as ClearedLogList by Entity | where LogClearCount > 10
references: https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/blob/63ff8eedc58e7df0d22eba05ca73c92b59a66634/Hunting Queries/Microsoft 365 Defender/Ransomware/Clearing of forensic evidence from event logs using wevtutil.yaml

rules.name: cve-2019-0808-c2
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Windows 7 zero-day for CVE-2019-0808
CVE-2019-0808 is a vulnerability that allows an attacker to escape the Windows security sandbox and run arbitrary code with admin privileges. This vulnerability affects Windows 7, Windows Server 2008, and Windows Server 2008 R2.
Exploits for CVE-2019-0808 were first observed as part of highly selective attacks using the Nufsys backdoor. Although the Nufsys-associated exploit was first described as a zero-day, the issue has since been patched.
The following query detects possible CVE-2019-0808 exploitation by reporting network communication associated with the Nufsys attacks.
References:
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-0808
https://portal.msrc.microsoft.com/security-guidance/advisory/CVE-2019-0808
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs' and ('Request URL' in ('luckluck.blog', 'fffun-video.biz') or 'Destination IP' = '63.141.233.82')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

Exploits for CVE-2019-0808 were first observed as part of highly selective attacks using the Nufsys backdoor. Although the Nufsys-associated exploit was first described as a zero-day, the issue has since been patched.

rules.name: cypherpunk-exclusive-commands
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Cypherpunk ransomware leaves wake of tampered AVs.
Cypherpunk is a human-operated ransomware campaign named after the unusual .cypherpunk extension given to encrypted files.
The query below surfaces commands that follow the distinctive pattern Cypherpunk operators would use to remotely execute code.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Parent Process Name' like 'psexe*') and ('Command Line' like '*Dvr /go*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: cypherpunk-remote-exec-w-psexesvc
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Cypherpunk ransomware leaves wake of tampered AVs.
Cypherpunk is a human-operated ransomware campaign named after the unusual .cypherpunk extension given to encrypted files. The attackers often used PSEXESVC, a service that helps the PsExe.exe utility run commands on a remote device. Both PSEXESVC and PsExe.exe are legitimate parts of Windows; however, they can be repurposed by attackers to perform malicious actions.
The query below can find instances of PSEXESVC being used to launch batch files, as often occurred in Cypherpunk attacks.
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Parent Process Name' like 'psexe*') and ('Command Line' like '*.bat*') and ('Command Line' like '*DisableIOAVProtection*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: deleting-data-w-cipher-tool
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Ransomware continues to hit healthcare, critical services. There is also a related blog.
In April of 2020, security researchers observed multiple ransomware campaigns using the same set of techniques.
The following query detects the use of the tool cipher.exe to delete indicators of malicious activity right before encrypting a drive.
The See also section below lists more queries related to techniques shared by these campaigns.
Reference - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2020/04/28/ransomware-groups-continue-to-target-healthcare-critical-services-heres-how-to-reduce-risk/
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Process Name' = 'cipher.exe') and ('Command Line' like '*/w*') | timestats span = 1minute distinctcount('Command Line') as CommandCount, unique('Command Line') as set_ProcessCommandLine by Entity | where CommandCount > 1

rules.name: Deletion of data on multiple drives using cipher exe

rules.name: detect-bluekeep-exploitation-attempts

Soon after its disclosure, the NSA issued a rare advisory about this vulnerability, out of concern that it could be used to quickly spread malware. Attackers have since used this vulnerability to install cryptocurrency miners on targets.
Microsoft has issued updates for this vulnerability, as well as guidance for protecting operating systems that we no longer support. Microsoft Defender ATP also contains behavioral detections for defending against this threat.
The following query detects devices with RDP connections that could be exploitation attempts.

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-0708
https://www.nsa.gov/News-Features/News-Stories/Article-View/Article/1865726/nsa-cybersecurity-advisory-patch-remote-desktop-services-on-legacy-versions-of/

https://portal.msrc.microsoft.com/security-guidance/advisory/CVE-2019-0708
https://support.microsoft.com/help/4500705/customer-guidance-for-cve-2019-0708
https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2019/11/07/the-new-cve-2019-0708-rdp-exploit-attacks-explained/

rules.name: detect-cyzfc-activity (1)
rules.description:
These queries was originally published in the threat analytics report, Attacks on gov't, think tanks, NGOs.
As described further in Analysis of cyberattack on U.S. think tanks, non-profits, public sector by unidentified attackers, there was a very large spear-phishing campaign launched in November 2019.
The attackers would gain access to a target by having the user click on a link to a compromised website and download a .zip archive.
Once established on a target's device, the attackers used a malicious DLL named cyzfc.dat to execute additional payloads. They would call a function in the malicious DLL via the legitimate Windows process, rundll32.exe, to connect directly to their command-and-control (C2) servers.
The following queries detect activity associated with the malicious DLL, cyzfc.dat., used in this campaign.
Reference - https://docs.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/rundll32
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Network Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Sysmon Network Logs') and ('Request URL' = 'pandorasong.com')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

The following query detects possible DoublePulsar execution events.
See Detect web server exploitation by DoublePulsar for a query that detects behaviors associated with campaigns that use DoublePulsar.

https://www.scmagazine.com/home/security-news/cybercrime/doublepulsar-malware-spreading-rapidly-in-the-wild-following-shadow-brokers-dump/
https://support.microsoft.com/help/4013389/title

rules.name: detect-exploitation-of-cve-2018-8653
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, CVE-2018-8653 scripting engine vulnerability.
CVE-2018-8653 is a remote code execution vulnerability found in the scripting engine for several releases of Internet Explorer. An attacker exploiting this CVE could use a malicious webpage to gain the same access rights as the currently logged-in user -- which is particularly problematic if the user is an administrator.
Microsoft has since addressed this vulnerability.
The following queries detect possible exploitation of this CVE.
References:
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-8653
https://portal.msrc.microsoft.com/security-guidance/advisory/CVE-2018-8653
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and ('Parent Process Name' = 'svchost.exe' and 'Command Line' like '*WinHttpAutoProxySvc*' and 'Process Name' != 'pacjsworker.exe' and 'Process Name' != 'svchost.exe' and 'Process Name' != 'WerFault.exe')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: detect-jscript-file-creation
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Emulation-evading JavaScripts.
Attackers in several ransomware campaigns have employed heavily obfuscated JavaScript code, in order to implant malware or execute malicious commands. The obfuscation is intended to help the code evade security systems and potentially escape sandbox environments.
The following query detects the creation of files with a .jse extension. Certain ransomware campaigns, such as Emotet, are known to employ encrypted JavaScript code that is saved to the target as .jse files.
See Detect potentially malicious .jse launch by File Explorer or Word for a similar technique.
Reference - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2017/11/06/mitigating-and-eliminating-info-stealing-qakbot-and-emotet-in-corporate-networks/
rules.oci_query: 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' and ('Process Name' like '*.jse')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: detect-malicious-rar-extraction
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, CVE-2018-15982 exploit attacks.
CVE-2018-15982 is an exploit of Adobe Flash Player, that allows for remote execution of arbitrary code. It has since been patched.
Actors have been observed using this vulnerability in targeted attacks. Exploits for CVE-2018-15982 have also been included in several exploit kits.
In some initial attacks exploiting CVE-2018-15982, attackers sent targets spear-phishing emails. The emails would include an attached RAR archive, which contained a lure document, as well as a second archive disguised as a .jpg file. Opening the document would automatically run an embedded Flash ActiveX control. This, in turn, would call a script containing the exploit. The exploit's ability to run arbitrary code would be employed to unpack and run a payload from the second archive. The payload is a backdoor used both to achieve persistance and for command and control.
The following query detects possible instances of a payload being extracted by the exploit.
References:
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-15982
https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/flash-player/apsb18-42.html
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'Windows Security Events') and ('Process Name' = 'cmd.exe') and ('Command Line' like '*set path=%ProgramFiles(x86)%\\WinRAR;C:\\Program Files\\WinRAR;*') and ('Command Line' like '*cd /d %~dp0 & rar.exe e -o+ -r -inul*.rar*')
rules.author: Upstream contributors

rules.name: doppelpaymer-procdump
rules.description:
This query was originally published in the threat analytics report, Doppelpaymer: More human-operated ransomware. There is also a related blog.
DoppelPaymer is ransomware that is spread manually by human operators. These operators have exhibited extensive knowledge of system administration and common network security misconfigurations. For example, they use SysInternal utilities such as ProcDump to dump credentials from LSASS. They often use these stolen credentials to turn off security software, run malicious commands, and spread malware throughout an organization.
The following query detects ProcDump being used to dump credentials from LSASS.
The See also section below lists links to other queries associated with DoppelPaymer.
References:
https://msrc-blog.microsoft.com/2019/11/20/customer-guidance-for-the-dopplepaymer-ransomware/
https://www.microsoft.com/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/DoppelPaymer!MTB&threatId=-2147205372
https://docs.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/procdump
https://docs.microsoft.com/windows-server/security/credentials-protection-and-management/configuring-additional-lsa-protection
rules.oci_query: ('Log Source' = 'Microsoft Defender Endpoint Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs') and (('Command Line' like '*lsass*' and ('Command Line' like '*-accepteula*' or 'Command Line' like '*-ma*')) or ('Process Name' in ('procdump.exe', 'procdump64.exe') and 'Command Line' like '*lsass*'))
